func_80000590.about: scheduler_add_client on the game's scheduler (0x80057188). Caller start_graphics (graphics start-up).
func_80000590.name: add_scheduler_client

func_800005BC.about: scheduler_remove_client on the game's scheduler (0x80057188). No converted callers.
func_800005BC.name: remove_scheduler_client

func_800005E0.about: Sends `task` to the queue 0x8005D448 (scheduler_graphics_queue), blocking. Caller func_80002DE4 (the graphics side). (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_800005E0.name: send_graphics_task

func_80000614.about: Returns the word at 0x80057404 (inside the game scheduler 0x80057188, at +0x27C, which create_scheduler clears). No converted callers. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_80000614.name: scheduler_value_57404

func_80000620.about: Returns the game's scheduler (0x80057188). Caller start_sound_system (audio start-up).
func_80000620.name: game_scheduler

func_8000062C.about: Copies `length` bytes from cartridge ROM address `rom_address` to `destination` in RAM by PI DMA, waiting until it is done (mod/src/gamefn.h: PI DMA).
func_8000062C.name: read_from_rom

func_8000071C.about: Sets *0x80057184, the most read_from_rom moves in one PI DMA, from the table at 0x800435F4 by `large` & 1: 0 -> 0x40 bytes, 1 -> 0x8000 (32 KB; the table read from the ROM), presumably so other PI users, the animation streams, get turns while the small pieces are in use. Callers func_800004D0, graphics_thread_main, func_80003180, run_game_loop (thread entries and boot). (2026-11-12: the name says what the code does; the reason is the reading.)
func_8000071C.name: set_rom_read_piece_size

func_800007AC.about: Calls the loaded overlay's entry at 0x800D9960 (every overlay is placed there; ovl_a's dispatches to run_front_end) with the four arguments it was given; the port routes it through rw_run_overlay. Caller run_game_loop (the main thread, four times).
func_800007AC.name: call_overlay_entry

func_800007D4.about:
Allocates `size` bytes from the game's heap and returns the block, or NULL when nothing fits.
The heap is 0x221800 bytes at 0x80194000, set up on first use (zeroed, one free block, tag 0xBABEFACE). Its free list of {next, size in 16-byte units} starts at *0x800435F0; the smallest free block that fits is used. The mod calls it the game's allocator (mod/src/logic.c).
func_800007D4.name: heap_alloc

func_8000093C.about: Gives a block from heap_alloc back to the heap. NULL is ignored, and so is a block whose header (the 16 bytes before it) lacks the tag 0xCAFE4ABE. The block goes back into the free list at *0x800435F0, which is kept in address order (mod/src/logic.c names this the game's free).
func_8000093C.name: heap_free

func_80000A90.about: Starts the frame scheduler `sc` (*0x8005D8D0): its client list (+0x260) empty, the retrace message queue (+0x40), the task queues 0x8005D448 (graphics), 0x8005D410 (audio), 0x8005D480, 0x8005D4B8, 0x8005D528, 0x8005D4F0; the VI manager in mode `vi_mode` (0x80053810 + mode x 0x50), screen black, retrace events every `retraces`, PRE-NMI (0xE) and SP / DP events (4, 9); a frame budget 0x8005D8D6 from the TV type (*0x80000300: 25 or 30) / retraces - 3; then its threads: the scheduler (0x80000E3C, priority 0x78), 0x80000F98 (0x6E) and 0x800010F4 (0x64) on queue 0x8005D410. libultra's sample osCreateScheduler is the model; which thread does audio and which graphics is inferred. (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: +0 = 1, *0x8005D8D0 = sc, +0x260 / +0x27C = 0, +0x20 = 4, the budget 25 (PAL, *0x80000300 0) or 30 divided by `retraces`.)
func_80000A90.name: create_scheduler

func_80000D38.about: Adds `client` to scheduler `sc`'s client list (+0x260), with interrupts masked: client +0 next, +4 its message queue `queue`; sends it a PRE-NMI message (sc + 0x20) at once when one has come (0x8005D8D4). libultra sample osScAddClient. Callers add_scheduler_client, scheduler_graphics_thread (func_800010F4), audio_add_scheduler_client (func_8002B2DC).
func_80000D38.name: scheduler_add_client

func_80000DB0.about: Unlinks `client` from scheduler `sc`'s client list (+0x260), with interrupts masked (libultra sample osScRemoveClient). Only caller remove_scheduler_client.
func_80000DB0.name: scheduler_remove_client

func_80000E30.about: Returns the message queue 0x8005D410 (made by create_scheduler and handed to its two worker threads). Caller run_audio_task (the audio code), hence the name. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: it returns the queue 0x8005D410 that create_scheduler makes, and its caller is the audio code).
func_80000E30.name: scheduler_audio_queue

func_80000E3C.about: The scheduler's event loop (`scheduler` the scheduler record, its queue at +0x40): on the retrace message 0x29A counts the retrace (+0x27C) and, unless the reset button has been pressed (0x8005D8D4 & 2), sends each client in the list +0x260 (scheduler_add_client) the scheduler; on the pre-NMI message 0x29D sets 0x8005D8D4 to 1 and sends each client the pre-NMI message (+0x20); once reset is under way it counts retraces down (from *0x8005D8D6) and calls after_pre_nmi. The shape of NuSystem's nuScEventHandler. (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed against the N64 SDK's sched.c (__scMain): the loop on the scheduler's queue (+0x40) for the retrace message 666 (0x29A, VIDEO_MSG) and the pre-NMI message 669 (0x29D, PRE_NMI_MSG), each passed to every client in the list +0x260).
func_80000E3C.name: scheduler_event_thread

func_80000F8C.about: Returns the message queue 0x8005D448 (made by create_scheduler). Only caller send_graphics_task. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: it returns the queue 0x8005D448, and its only caller is send_graphics_task).
func_80000F8C.name: scheduler_graphics_queue

func_80000F98.about: The scheduler's audio task loop: takes each task from the queue 0x8005D410 and runs it, or (once reset is under way, 0x8005D8D4 & 2) just answers it on the task's own queue (+0x50, message +0x54). The shape of NuSystem's nuScExecuteAudio. (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed from the lifted C++: it receives each audio task from 0x8005D410, yields a running graphics task (osSpTaskYield) and runs the audio one (osSpTaskLoad / osSpTaskStartGo)).
func_80000F98.name: scheduler_audio_thread

func_800010F4.about: The scheduler's graphics task loop: adds itself as a retrace client (scheduler_add_client on *0x8005D8D0, queue 0x8005D528), then takes each graphics task from 0x8005D448 and runs it (func_800012B0, with the interrupt mask), or answers it at once when reset is under way (0x8005D8D4 & 2). The shape of NuSystem's nuScExecuteGraphics. (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed from the lifted C++: it registers as a retrace client (scheduler_add_client), then receives each graphics task from 0x8005D448 and runs it (osSpTaskLoad / osSpTaskStartGo), waiting while an audio task holds the RSP).
func_800010F4.name: scheduler_graphics_thread

func_800012B0.about: Waits until the frame buffer of graphics task `task` (its word +0xC) is neither the one shown now nor the next: first empties the retrace queue 0x8005D528 without blocking (osRecvMesg until it returns -1), then, while osViGetCurrentFramebuffer or osViGetNextFramebuffer gives that buffer, waits for the next retrace message. Caller scheduler_graphics_thread, before it runs each graphics task. A mod hooks its entry. (2026-11-14, rest100: from the lifted C++.)
func_800012B0.name: wait_framebuffer_free

func_80001340.about: Graphics start-up; the first call only (*0x80043614 == 1): reads 0xA0 bytes from ROM 0x57270 into a heap block (*0x800BD94C), makes the graphics queue 0x80060AA8 and adds it as a scheduler client (add_scheduler_client), starts thread 3 at 0x80003138 (priority 0x46), copies the VI mode for the TV type (*0x80000300: 1 NTSC 0x80054990, 2 MPAL 0x800549E0, else PAL 0x80054A30) to 0x80060B40, patches it for 480-wide output (0x1E0, 0x300, 0x3C0) and sets it with special features 0x6A and the screen black, makes two 0x2F58-byte graphics task records (*0x8005D8E0, +0x2F30 the queue, +0x38 message 2), a zeroed 0x977A0-byte block (*0x80060B90, frame buffers by size) and reset_colour_tints. Every call clears the draw list counts 0x800619B0/B2/B4. Callers run_game_loop (boot), start_front_end (front end set-up), set_up_match_area. (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: the first-call flag *0x80043614 cleared, heap_alloc(0xA0) + read_from_rom(0x57270), osCreateMesgQueue 0x80060AA8 (16), add_scheduler_client, osCreateThread(0x8005E8F0, 3, 0x80003138, .., 0x46), the two one-message queues 0x80060B00 / 0x80060B20, osStartThread, the VI mode copy (0x50 bytes) by *0x80000300.)
func_80001340.name: start_graphics

func_800015A4.about: Stores `persp_norm` as camera `camera`'s perspective normalisation (s16 at +4), the scale gu_perspective_f hands back for G_PERSPNORM. Callers set_camera_view, set_camera_view_rolled, set_camera_projection_and_view (whose abouts call it the normalisation).
func_800015A4.name: set_camera_persp_norm

func_800015AC.about: Does nothing, though the game still calls it. Probably what is left of something removed before release. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_800015AC.name: empty_800015AC

func_800015B4.about: Starts a bone afresh: its flags byte +0x18 (0x80 = not drawn) set to `flags`, +0x19 and +0x1A cleared, its links and draw object (+0x0 to +0x14) cleared, and its place (+0x1C) set to (x, y, z) by make_translation_matrix (func_80038AC0). set_up_bone passes its kind as the flags.
func_800015B4.name: init_bone

func_8000161C.about: Adds `bone`'s draw object (+0x14) to the frame's draw list (the words from 0x805EA9A0, *0x800619B2 of them) unless it's there already: the list is searched, and when the object isn't found it is put at the end and the count goes up. The model builders call it for each bone they set up (27 callers). (2026-11-12: renamed from find_in_draw_list: the code shows what happens when it isn't found.)
func_8000161C.name: add_to_draw_list_once

func_80001684.about: Makes sure `bone` has a draw object (+0x14; a new one from new_scene_record (func_8000176C) if not), sets the bone's byte +0x1B to `value` and clears the object's mesh. mod/src/announce.c: a bone's draw object.
func_80001684.name: give_bone_draw_object

func_800016E4.about: Makes a new record (from new_scene_record) for one of a part's vertex groups and returns it; join_part_to_bones fills a part's two group records (+0x28, +0x2C) with it (mod/NOTES.md traces the chain). (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: join_part_to_bones (confirmed) fills a part's two vertex-group records (+0x28, +0x2C) with it).
func_800016E4.name: new_vertex_group_record

func_80001738.about: Adds another draw object (new_scene_record) to `bone`: its +4 the bone, +8 the old first one, and the bone's +0x14 points to it. No converted callers.
func_80001738.name: add_bone_draw_object

func_8000176C.about: Hands out a 0xB8-byte scene record (for bones and draw objects) from the block made on the heap at boot, and returns it in v0. m2c made it void although its callers use the pointer; that trap is described in mod/NOTES.md.
func_8000176C.name: new_scene_record

func_800017D0.about: Sets draw object `object`'s centre (+0xC / +0x10 / +0x14) to the average of its bone's mesh points (the bone at +4: points +0xC, s16 x, y, z, 16 bytes each, count +0x1B); left as it is when the bone has no points. Caller centre_bone_draw_objects.
func_800017D0.name: centre_draw_object_on_mesh

func_800018A4.about: centre_draw_object_on_mesh (func_800017D0) on each draw object in `bone`'s chain (+0x14, linked by +8): each one's +0xC/+0x10/+0x14 set to the average of the bone's mesh points (bone +0xC, count +0x1B, 16 bytes each). Only caller give_bone_draw_object; shade_bone_tree uses the centre.
func_800018A4.name: centre_bone_draw_objects

func_800018E0.about: Splits a tint channel `value` (0x80 neutral) into a pair: 0x80 and up give `amount` = value x 2 and `sign` 0xFF; below, `amount` = ~(value x 2) and `sign` 0. Only caller set_colour_tint.
func_800018E0.name: split_tint_value

func_80001918.about: Sets tint `slot` (0-3; `kind` must be 0 or 1) to the RGBA bytes at `colour`: each channel split (split_tint_value) into 0x80062B68 and 0x80062B88 + slot x 4, in the frame's copy (*0x80043610 x 0x10). Callers reset_colour_tints, set_current_colour_tint.
func_80001918.name: set_colour_tint

func_80001A04.about: Sets all four tint slots of both kinds to neutral (0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0xFF). Caller start_graphics (graphics start-up). (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_80001A04.name: reset_colour_tints

func_80001A78.about: set_colour_tint with the kind kept at 0x80043611. Callers set_screen_tint, clear_screen_tints. (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: set_colour_tint(*0x80043611, slot & 0xFF, colour).)
func_80001A78.name: set_current_colour_tint

func_80001AA4.about: Shades the bone tree from `bone` by a point light: keeps strength (*0x80062B50), base level (*0x80062B54) and the light's place (`place`, 3 floats, at 0x80062B58) and runs shade_bone_tree. Callers func_800E1E60, pose_and_light_scene_actor (front end).
func_80001AA4.name: light_bone_tree

func_80001B10.about: For each bone from `bone` with a draw object and +0x1A set: the light's direction from the bone's centre (draw object +0xC..+0x14 through the bone's matrix at +0x5C, transform_point, gu_normalize), then for each draw object in its chain (+8) each vertex's direction from the centre; the vertex's alpha byte (+0xF) = base + strength x dot product when lit, else base, at most 255 (light_bone_tree's settings at 0x80062B50..). Recurses over the tree. Only caller light_bone_tree.
func_80001B10.name: shade_bone_tree

func_80001E08.about: Writes `left` x `right` into `result`, 4x4 floats in rows (each of result's rows is that row of left through right). The camera's view and projection are combined with it (mod/src/announce.c, func_80001580).
func_80001E08.name: multiply_matrices

func_8000214C.about: 1 when `point` is drawn left of `point_2` on screen, else 0: each point's x through the camera matrix over its depth, compared with `<` (mod/src/tron.c mirrors it as hc_sides; build_ring_side_table hands it a ring side's two ends). (2026-11-14, fablenames: renamed from ring_side_ends and confirmed: the lifted C++ returns 1 when the first point is drawn left of the second, else 0 -- each point's x through the camera matrix (the 16 floats at 0x80062BA8, fields.json camera_matrix: elements 0 / 4 / 8 / 12) over its depth (elements 2 / 6 / 10 / 14, plus the double 0x80055818), compared with `<`. mod/src/tron.c's hc_sides is the same sum written out: px = vp[0] x + vp[4] y + vp[8] z + vp[12], pw = vp[2] x + vp[6] y + vp[10] z + vp[14] + 1000, sx[0] < sx[1]. The old name called it the side's ends; it is the test on any two points, and build_ring_side_table hands it a side's two ends)) (2026-11-14, names083: the first sentence rewritten to say what the dated note above found; the old one gave the reading the note corrects.)
func_8000214C.name: point_is_left_of_on_screen

func_800022D8.about: For each draw object in the frame's table (*0x805EA9A0[i], count *0x800619B2): unless its node's +0x18 & 0x80FF0000, the node's matrix (+0x5C) times the camera 0x80062BA8 into +0x9C, its centre (+0xC..+0x14) transformed into +0x18..+0x20 and +0x28 = (z + radius +0x24) x a constant + the screen distance sqrt(x^2 + y^2); otherwise +0x28 = radius x the constant. Callers func_800E1E60 (the match frame) and the front end's frame (draw_front_end_frame, func_800DA568). Reading: a depth for sorting / culling. (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: multiply_matrices(node + 0x5C, 0x80062BA8, node + 0x9C), transform_point of +0xC..+0x14, +0x28 = (+0x24 + z) x the double 0x80055820 + square_root(x^2 + y^2).)
func_800022D8.name: compute_draw_object_depths

func_80002400.about: Sorts the frame's draw items far to near for the camera by their key (made by compute_draw_object_depths (func_800022D8) from each item's centre), so they are drawn back to front: the game has no depth buffer for these. mod/src/tron.c, mod/NOTES.md.
func_80002400.name: sort_draw_items

func_800025B0.about: Moves the frame's draw objects whose tag byte (0x800619B8[i]) is `tag` and whose first word is `kind` into the build queue (0x805EF4A0[*0x800619B4++], the tag set to 0xFF), converting each linked node's float matrix (node +4 +0x9C, along +8) to a fixed-point one in the node at +0x38 + `buffer` x 64 (gu_mtx_float_to_fixed; kind 1 only when func_800024F8 agrees, other kinds also copy the node's +0x10 into +0x34). Caller queue_frame_draw_passes (eight tags in turn). (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed from the lifted C++: the draw objects whose tag byte and first word match moved into the build queue).
func_800025B0.name: queue_draw_objects_by_tag

func_80002DE4.about: Finishes the frame's display list and sends it to the RSP: writes the full-sync and end-of-list commands (0xE9, 0xDF) at `list_end`, fills in the frame's graphics task -- boot microcode 0x80040380, one of two microcode pairs by the low half of `microcode_choice` (0x800410B0 / 0x80054FD0 when 0, else 0x80042450 / 0x800553F0), the list from *`list_start` and its size, the buffers from rw_dlbase_v0_v1 -- with the message 0x63 or 3 by the low half of a2, writes the data cache back (func_80034440) and hands the task to send_graphics_task; then flips the frame index 0x80043610 between 0 and 1. The fields' meanings follow libultra's OSTask, hence a guess. (2026-11-14, rest100: from the lifted C++.)
func_80002DE4.name: send_frame_graphics_task

func_80002FA4.about: Builds a frame's display list: the picture the game draws each frame (mod/src/draw.c adds the arcade's words to it).
func_80002FA4.name: build_frame

func_80003044.about: Clears the word handed to the graphics thread (0x80060B3C), which graphics_thread_main (func_80003138) checks after each message. Callers start_front_end, set_up_match_area. (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: the one store.)
func_80003044.name: clear_graphics_task

func_80003050.about: Hands frame `frame` to the graphics thread and waits for its answer: *0x80060B3C = the frame, a message to the graphics thread's queue 0x80060B00 (osSendMesg, blocking; graphics_thread_main waits there), then osRecvMesg on 0x80060B20 (blocking). wait_for_graphics_thread is the same with no frame. Where the game threads park at the end of a frame until the next one (func_800E1E60's call; mod/NOTES.md traced a freeze there). (2026-11-12, names2: renamed from wait_for_frame_end; read from the lifted C++.)
func_80003050.name: hand_frame_to_graphics_thread

func_80003094.about: The same as wait_for_graphics_thread (func_800030F4), a second copy: clears 0x80060B3C, messages the graphics thread (0x80060B00) and waits for its answer (0x80060B20). Callers update_slot_loading, start_front_end, wait_graphics_count_frames.
func_80003094.name: wait_for_graphics_thread_80003094

func_800030D8.about: Just calls wait_for_graphics_thread. Callers run_front_end, free_match_scene.
func_800030D8.name: call_wait_for_graphics_thread

func_800030F4.about: Hands the graphics thread a message (queue 0x80060B00) with no frame (0x80060B3C cleared first) and waits for its answer (queue 0x80060B20): graphics_thread_main answers that queue after its frame request, so this returns once the thread has come round its loop -- the game's way to wait until the frame being drawn is done before changing what it draws (model loads, scene changes and wait_menu_widgets_gone call it; 23 callers). (Confirmed 2026-11-12 against graphics_thread_main.)
func_800030F4.name: wait_for_graphics_thread

func_80003138.about: The graphics thread's loop: waits for a frame request (queue 0x80060B00); with a frame (*0x80060B3C) points it at the next of the two frame buffers (0x80638400 / 0x80600000 in turn) and gathers its draw objects (queue_frame_draw_passes, func_80002730), then answers on 0x80060B20; between frames reads the scheduler queue 0x80060AA8 (1 retrace, 2 a task done, 4 pre-NMI: 0x80043612 = 1, osViSetYScale(1), osViBlack, stop_sound_and_mute) and builds the frame's display lists (build_frame) for the queued objects (*0x800619B4) while fewer than two tasks are out; then swaps the buffer index.
func_80003138.name: graphics_thread_main

func_800033B8.about: Zeroes the two frame buffers, 0x80638400 and 0x80600000 (0xE100 words each). No converted caller.
func_800033B8.name: clear_frame_buffers

func_80003420.about: Starts the sound system at boot (caller run_game_loop): reads five pieces of the ROM into heap blocks (read_from_rom, func_8000062C): 0x016F32A0 (*0x80062BF0), 0x01855F90 (*0x80062BF4), 0x01858030 (*0x80062BF8), 0x01965C50 (*0x80062BFC), 0x01967410 (*0x80062C00); starts the sound player (init_sound_driver, func_80026F60) with a configuration on the stack (the game scheduler, 0x50 and 0x18 counts, heap 0x800BD960 of 0x1C000 bytes, output rate 0x7080 = 28800, and others); both volume settings 0x7F; then two banks: *0x80062BF4 with wave data *0x80062BF8 (ROM 0x0185EDB0) and *0x80062BFC (the bank start_music_from_bank plays from) with *0x80062C00 (ROM 0x01969880), through set_up_sample_bank (func_80027AD8) / set_bank_wave_data (func_80027D50) / set_up_sound_effect_bank (func_80027CA0). Which block is a bank, a wave table or the sequence data is inferred from the call pattern. (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: the five ROM reads into heap blocks and the sound player start with the stack configuration in that order.)
func_80003420.name: start_sound_system

func_80003644.about: Starts `sound` (start_sound_from_bank) unless sound is off (0x80043626); returns its handle or 0. No converted callers.
func_80003644.name: start_sound_unless_off

func_8000367C.about: Plays sound `sound` (start_sound_effect with the five values, under the names that function's entry gives them: volume, pan, reuse, priority) unless the game's sound is off (0x80043626 not 0); returns its handle, or 0. play_menu_sound calls it with 0x80, 0x80, 1, -1, taken to be full volume, centre pan, reuse and the bank's own priority.
func_8000367C.name: play_sound

func_800036DC.about: Stops every sound at once (stop_all_sounds_over(3, 0)), waits until none is playing (count_playing_sounds), then sets the sound-off flag (0x80043626: play_sound plays nothing while it's set). Four callers in the boot / mode switch code (graphics_thread_main (func_80003138) ...).
func_800036DC.name: stop_sound_and_mute

func_80003714.about: Stereo on (`stereo` not 0) or mono (set_mono_sound of whether it is 0). Callers func_80111158, store_screen_17_19_options (init_menu_screen_17's code); the arcade (mod/src/logic.c GF_80003714) calls it from the byte at 0x800A946C, so that byte is the sound option (nonzero mono).
func_80003714.name: set_stereo

func_80003734.about: Whether sound `handle` is still playing on any channel (sound_channel_count > 0). Callers stop_sound, play_crowd_cue, play_wrestler_sound.
func_80003734.name: sound_is_playing

func_80003754.about: Unless sound is off (0x80043626): when `song` is not 0, stops the music (stop_music, func_800037BC), starts `song` (play_song, func_80027214) keeping its handle at 0x80043620 and the music level 0x80043624 at 0x80; returns the music's handle. Caller func_80017C64. Settles set_music_volume's sound as the music.
func_80003754.name: start_music

func_80003848.about: Unless sound is off: stops the music, plays from the bank *0x80062BFC (set_next_sound_bank) start_sound_effect (func_80027514) with the five values given (the second kept as the music level 0x80043624), keeping the handle at 0x80043620 as the music. No converted callers. (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed from the lifted C++: stop_music, set_next_sound_bank with the music bank (fields.json _variables music_bank), start_sound_effect with the five values, the handle kept as sound_handle and the level as music_level).
func_80003848.name: start_music_from_bank

func_8000390C.about: Whether the music (handle 0x80043620) still plays (sound_channel_count); forgets the handle when it doesn't. Caller func_80017C64.
func_8000390C.name: music_is_playing

Callers start_sound_system and start_front_end (the front end starting, after the settings are loaded); that `setting` is an options volume is inferred.

func_8000399C.about: The setting apply_volume_setting last applied (high byte of 0x80062C04). No converted callers. (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: apply_volume_setting (confirmed) keeps setting << 8 at 0x80062C04, and this returns its high byte).

func_800039B0.about: The music's level (0x80043624, set by start_music and set_music_volume). No converted callers.
func_800039B0.name: music_level

func_800039BC.about: Unless sound is off (0x80043626), sets the music's volume (the handle start_music keeps at 0x80043620; stop_music stops it) to `volume` held to 0..0x100 (0 or less resets the stored level 0x80043624 to 0x100 and uses 0), only when it changed from 0x80043624 (set_sound_volume). Callers func_80017C64 (a song played), run_pause_menu. (2026-11-12, names2: renamed from set_main_sound_volume -- 0x80043620 is the music's handle, as start_music and stop_music show.)

func_80003A90.about: The setting apply_second_volume_setting last applied (high byte of 0x80062C06). No converted callers. (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: apply_second_volume_setting keeps setting << 8 at 0x80062C06, and this returns its high byte).
func_80003A90.name: second_volume_setting

func_80003AB0.about: Reads the ROM file table (0x1300C bytes at ROM 0x016C31D8) into *0x80062C10 and works out each of the 0x4C02 files' sizes into *0x80062C14: the gap to the next file's offset, or (for an entry with bit 0 set) the 4-byte size read from the file's start; files sit at ROM 0x1BD150 + offset. Caller run_game_loop.
func_80003AB0.name: load_file_table

func_80003D64.about: Unpacks LZSS-packed data from `source` into `destination` (mod/src/gamefn.h; mod/src/files.c unpacks the game's files with it).
func_80003D64.name: unpack_lzss

func_80003E90.about: Which of 8 groups of 128 pages Flash page `page` (taken mod 0x400) is in: (page & 0x3FF) / 128. Used by flash_sector_distance and next_flash_write_page; reading the groups as the Flash's erase sectors is a guess.
func_80003E90.name: flash_page_sector

func_80003EA4.about: The first page of Flash sector `sector` (taken mod 8): (sector & 7) << 7. Only caller move_flash_write_to_next_sector; the reverse of flash_page_sector.
func_80003EA4.name: flash_sector_first_page

func_80003EB0.about: How many page groups (flash_page_sector) `to_page` is ahead of `from_page`, going round the 8: (sector(to_page) - sector(from_page)) mod 8. Callers are the Flash save's writers (write_flash_header (func_80004534), write_save_block_to_flash (func_8000461C), write_save_block_if_changed (func_80004858)).
func_80003EB0.name: flash_sector_distance

func_80003F18.about: Sets 0x80062FE4, the page next_flash_write_page won't pass (taken to be the oldest still needed), from the header. Only caller map_flash_save_blocks. (2026-11-13, names5: renamed from set_flash_oldest_page: the name now says what the code makes of the word (next_flash_write_page gives -1 when the next page starts the sector of 0x80062FE4); that it is the oldest page still needed stays the about's reading).
func_80003F18.name: set_flash_stop_page

func_80003F24.about: Sets 0x80062FE6 from the header; move_flash_write_to_next_sector starts from its sector, so it is taken to be the last page written. Only caller map_flash_save_blocks. (2026-11-13, names5: renamed from set_flash_last_page: the name now says what the code makes of the word (move_flash_write_to_next_sector starts the writes at the sector after the one 0x80062FE6 is in); that it is the last page written stays the about's reading).
func_80003F24.name: set_flash_resume_page

func_80003F30.about: Sets the next Flash page to write (0x80062FE8, next_flash_write_page's). Only caller map_flash_save_blocks.
func_80003F30.name: set_flash_next_page

func_80003F3C.about: Moves the next page to write (0x80062FE8) to the start of the sector after the one 0x80062FE6 is in (flash_page_sector + 1, flash_sector_first_page) and returns it. Caller func_80004EE8; mod/gen/checksave.py stubs it.
func_80003F3C.name: move_flash_write_to_next_sector

func_80003F84.about: Moves the Flash save's next page to write (0x80062FE8) on by one, wrapping to 0 at 0x3FE, and returns the page it was; returns -1 instead when the page starts a group (a multiple of 128) that is the group of 0x80062FE4 (taken to be the oldest page still needed). The pages are used in turn round the Flash (a rotating log of saves); that reading is inferred from these helpers. (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: -1 only when the page is at a 128-page boundary and flash_page_sector of it equals that of *0x80062FE4; otherwise the page returned and *0x80062FE8 moved on, 0 after 0x3FD.)
func_80003F84.name: next_flash_write_page

func_8000401C.about: XORs together the 32 words of a block, starting from -1, with the second word counted as zero. It's zeroed for the sum and put back, so it's probably where the checksum itself is kept. (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: word 1 saved and zeroed, the 32 words XORed from -1, word 1 put back; callers write_flash_page, read_flash_page.)
func_8000401C.name: block_checksum

func_80004054.about: Writes the 128-byte write buffer (0x80062EA8, its checksum put at +4 first by block_checksum) to Flash page `page` (under 0x3FE): osFlashWriteBuffer then osFlashWriteArray (func_80034440 first, taken to be the cache write-back), then reads the page back (read_flash_page) and compares the 0x80 bytes (compare_bytes, func_80036600). Returns 0 when it all matched, -1 otherwise. Callers are the save's writers (write_flash_header (func_80004534), write_save_block_to_flash (func_8000461C), write_save_block_if_changed (func_80004858), format_flash_save (func_80004CE4)).
func_80004054.name: write_flash_page

func_80004148.about: Reads 128-byte page `page` (under 0x3FE) of the cartridge's Flash into the read buffer 0x80062DA8 (osFlashReadArray, waiting on the queue 0x80062FC8; func_80034310 first, taken to be the cache invalidate), trying up to 8 times until block_checksum of it matches the checksum stored at its +4. Returns 0 when good, -1 otherwise. Callers: write_flash_page (to check what it wrote) and the save's readers (map_flash_save_blocks (func_8000423C) ...).
func_80004148.name: read_flash_page

func_8000423C.about: Builds the map of the save's blocks on the Flash: sets the write positions from the header (set_flash_stop_page (func_80003F18) / F24 / F30 with +0x1C and +0x1E), clears the 0x140-entry map at 0x80062FF0 to -1, then follows the chain of pages back from the header's last page (0x80062CA8: each page's +0 the page before it, +2 its block number) noting the newest page of each block. Returns -1 when the header is empty. Callers open_flash_save, func_80004EE8; mod/gen/checksave.py hooks it. 'Chain' and 'block' are read from the code; the layout of a block's 0x78 data bytes isn't traced. (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: set_flash_stop_page(*0x80062CC4), set_flash_resume_page(*0x80062CC6), set_flash_next_page(last + 1), the 0x140 halfwords at 0x80062FF0 set to -1, then read_flash_page down the chain from *0x80062CA8; -1 when the header words at 0x80062CB0 are 0 and the next under 2.)
func_8000423C.name: map_flash_save_blocks

func_80004368.about: Checks a Flash header page: its word at +0x10 is 0x80721 and its two 8-byte strings at +8 and +0x18 match the game's at 0x80043630 and 0x80043638. Returns 0 when valid, -1 when not. Only caller find_flash_header.
func_80004368.name: flash_header_is_valid

func_800043D0.about: Reads every Flash page (0 to 0x3FD, read_flash_page) and keeps, at 0x80062CA8, the header page (kind +2 = 0x4000, passing flash_header_is_valid (func_80004368)) with the highest generation number (+8); returns 0 when one was found, -1 otherwise. Callers open_flash_save, func_80004EE8 (the save write). mod/gen/checksave.py hooks it. (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: zero_bytes(0x80062CA8, 0x80), pages 0-0x3FD read with read_flash_page, a valid one (flash_header_is_valid of 0x80062DB0, kind 0x4000) with a higher number copied over (0x80 bytes) and 0 returned.)
func_800043D0.name: find_flash_header

func_800044D8.about: Erases the Flash sector holding page `page` (osFlashSectorErase), trying up to 4 times while it fails; returns the last result (-1 failed). Callers write_flash_header, write_save_block_to_flash, write_save_block_if_changed, when the next page to write starts a new 128-page sector.
func_800044D8.name: erase_flash_sector

func_80004534.about: Writes the save header (0x80062CA8, with the page it goes to at +0x16 of 0x80062CB0) to the next free Flash page (next_flash_write_page), only while that stays within 4 page groups of `first_page` (flash_sector_distance) or erase_flash_sector (func_800044D8) allows; tries the next page when a write fails. Returns the result of the write, -1 when no page was found. Callers write_save_to_flash, commit_save_to_flash (func_800049E8).
func_80004534.name: write_flash_header

func_8000461C.about: Writes save block `block` (0x78 bytes of the save image *0x80062C20 at block x 0x78) to the next free Flash page: the write buffer 0x80062EA8 gets the page before it in the chain (`previous`, +0) and the block number (+2) and the data at +8; pages are taken from next_flash_write_page, a new sector erased first (erase_flash_sector) unless it would come within 4 sectors of `oldest` (flash_sector_distance), and write_flash_page retried on the next page when it fails. Returns the page written, or -1. Caller write_save_to_flash. The roles of the second and third arguments follow write_save_block_if_changed, which does the same with 0x80062FE4. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_8000461C.name: write_save_block_to_flash

func_80004714.about: Writes the whole save image to the Flash as a chain of pages: the block count (*0x80062C24 + 0x77) / 120 into 0x80062CD0, block 0 written first (write_save_block_to_flash(0, 0x2000 = no page before it, `arg0`)) and its page kept in 0x80062CC4, then blocks 1 .. count - 1, each chained to the page written before it; when all went well the last page into the header 0x80062CA8 (kind +2 = 0x4000) and the header written (write_flash_header), its result returned; -1 on a failed write. Callers func_80004EE8 (the save write) and the mod's copy; mod/gen/checksave.py hooks it to see what would be written. (2026-11-12, names3: renamed from write_save_data and confirmed from the lifted C++: every block goes out, so it is the whole image; the open question of the old about is settled.)
func_80004714.name: write_save_to_flash

func_80004858.about: Writes save block `block` to the Flash only when it changed: reads its newest page (the map 0x80062FF0[block], read_flash_page) and compares it with the image's bytes (compare_bytes over at most 0x78, the image size *0x80062C24 cut at the end); if equal returns that page unchanged, else writes it like write_save_block_to_flash with `previous` as the chain link and 0x80062FE4 as the oldest page. Returns the page, -1 on failure. Only caller commit_save_to_flash.
func_80004858.name: write_save_block_if_changed

func_800049E8.about: Writes the save image to the Flash: for each of its (size + 0x77) / 0x78 blocks (count kept at header +0x28, 0x80062CD0) write_save_block_if_changed, chaining each written page to the previous one; when any page changed, the header (0x80062CA8: +0 the last page, +2 kind 0x4000) goes out with write_flash_header. Returns 0 when nothing changed, the header write's result, or -1. Caller func_80004EE8; mod/gen/checksave.py hooks it as a write.
func_800049E8.name: commit_save_to_flash

func_80004B7C.about: Reads Flash page `page` (read_flash_page) and copies its data (from +8, at most 0x78 bytes, `length`) into save block `block` of the image (*0x80062C20 + block x 0x78). Returns the read's result (-1 failed). Only caller load_save_from_flash.
func_80004B7C.name: read_save_block_from_flash

func_80004C28.about: Opens the Flash save for the image `image` of `size` bytes (kept at 0x80062C20 / 0x80062C24; mod/src/save.c: *0x80062C20 is the save image): on first use osFlashInit and the Flash's message queue (0x80062FC8); then the newest header (find_flash_header), formatting the Flash when there is none (format_flash_save), and the map of where each block of the save is (map_flash_save_blocks). Returns -1 when both failed. Callers open_save_image, create_new_save.
func_80004C28.name: open_flash_save

func_80004CCC.about: Clears the Flash save's image pointer and size (0x80062C20, 0x80062C24) and returns 0. No converted callers. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_80004CCC.name: forget_flash_save_image

func_80004CE4.about: Erases the whole Flash (osFlashAllErase) and writes a fresh header (0x80062CA8: generation 0, +4 = 1, the value 0x80721, two 8-byte strings from 0x80043630 / 0x80043638, kind 0x4000 at +2) to the first page that takes it (write_flash_page). Returns 0, or -1 / the erase's error. Callers open_flash_save, create_new_save. (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: osFlashAllErase, then the header words 0x80062CB0 = 0, +4 = 1, 0x80062CC0 = 0x80721, the two 8-byte strings into +8 / +0x18, +0x20 = 0, kind 0x80062CAA = 0x4000, and the page loop.)
func_80004CE4.name: format_flash_save

func_80004DD8.about: Fills the save image (*0x80062C20) from the Flash: returns 1 for a blank save (header generation 0 and +0xC = 1), else reads every block from its newest page (the map 0x80062FF0, block count at header +0x28, as commit_save_to_flash keeps it), last first, the last one cut to the image size's remainder (read_save_block_from_flash). Returns -1 on failure or no image, else the last read's result. Caller open_save_image.
func_80004DD8.name: load_save_from_flash

func_80004FE0.about: Whether the Game Boy cartridge read by gb_pak_read_id is the one the game talks to: the 11-byte title at 0x8006330C (id + 0x34) equals the string at 0x80043650 and the company code (id + 0x44) is '78' (0x3738, the same company as the Controller Pak note). Returns 1 or 0. Only caller open_transfer_pak.
func_80004FE0.name: gb_cart_is_ours

func_80005034.about: Opens the Transfer Pak on `channel`: takes the SI lock (take_shared_lock, kept at 0x8004365C), gb_pak_init on the pfs 0x80063270, gb_pak_read_id (id 0x800632D8, status 0x8006332C), checks the cartridge is the game's partner (gb_cart_is_ours) and the connector (gb_pak_check_connector (func_80039430), taken to be osGbpakCheckConnector). Returns 0 when ready, 4 for another cartridge, bit 0 on an error (result in 0x80063328); the lock is given back when the init fails. Callers read_gb_cart_ram, write_gb_cart_ram.
func_80005034.name: open_transfer_pak

func_8000512C.about: When the Transfer Pak is open (0x8004365C), turns its cartridge off (gb_pak_power(pfs, 0)) and gives back the SI lock (release_shared_lock). Callers read_gb_cart_ram, write_gb_cart_ram.
func_8000512C.name: close_transfer_pak

func_8000516C.about: Whether `address` and `size` are both multiples of 32, the address not negative and address + size at most 0xBFFF (the end of a Game Boy cartridge's RAM window, 0xA000-0xBFFF). Callers read_gb_cart_ram, write_gb_cart_ram.
func_8000516C.name: gb_ram_range_ok

func_800051A8.about: Prepares the Game Boy cartridge's RAM through the Transfer Pak: writes 0 to 0x4000 (RAM bank 0) and, when that works, 0x0A to 0x0000 (the cartridge's RAM enable), 32-byte writes from 0x80063330 (gb_pak_read_write). Returns the last result. Callers read_gb_cart_ram, write_gb_cart_ram.
func_800051A8.name: enable_gb_cart_ram

func_80005248.about: Reads `size` bytes of the Game Boy cartridge's memory at `address` into `buffer` through the Transfer Pak on `channel` (0-3): gb_ram_range_ok (else 0x80), open_transfer_pak, enable_gb_cart_ram, gb_pak_read_write(read), gb_pak_get_status (bit 0 clear: 0x10), close_transfer_pak. Returns 0 or error bits (8 a pak error). Caller read_gb_save.
func_80005248.name: read_gb_cart_ram

func_80005390.about: The writing twin of read_gb_cart_ram: writes `size` bytes from `buffer` to the Game Boy cartridge at `address` through the Transfer Pak on `channel` (gb_pak_read_write with flag 1). Caller write_gb_save_flags.
func_80005390.name: write_gb_cart_ram

func_800054C0.about: The Transfer Pak code's last libultra result (0x80063328). Callers editor_top_page_run, show_page_dialog and an ovl_d copy.
func_800054C0.name: transfer_pak_result

func_800054CC.about: The Transfer Pak's last status byte (0x8006332C, from gb_pak_read_id / gb_pak_get_status). No converted callers.
func_800054CC.name: transfer_pak_status

func_800054E0.about: atan(x) in radians by an 8-term continued fraction; above 1 or below -1 it works on 1 / x and returns pi / 2 (0x80055840) or -pi / 2 (0x80055848) less that. Only caller arc_tangent_2, whose about calls it the arc tangent.
func_800054E0.name: arc_tangent

func_800055D8.about: The angle (radians) of the direction (y, x), as atan2(y, x): 0 or pi when y is 0, else from the arc tangent of x / y (arc_tangent, func_800054E0) with the quadrant fixed.
func_800055D8.name: arc_tangent_2

func_8000567C.about: Returns a float without its sign. The mod has the same as nm_fabs (mod/src/skel.c).
func_8000567C.name: float_abs

func_800056A4.about: Returns a number without its sign.
func_800056A4.name: absolute_value

func_800056C0.about: Starts the controllers: points each of the 4 controller records (0x8051C140, 0xC each, +0) at its status (0x80063388 + 4n), osContInit (bit pattern of those present to 0x80063538), cont_set_channels(4), makes the SI lock queue 0x80063368 (take_shared_lock's), then for each channel init_rumble_pak, stops the motor when there is one (func_80039890, taken to be __osMotorAccess) and clears its rumble state (0x8006353C, 0x80063540, 0x80063544); gives the lock back. Returns osContInit's result. Caller run_game_loop.
func_800056C0.name: init_controllers

func_80005818.about: Updates each controller's state, 0xC bytes each at 0x8009EDA0: +4 buttons held, +6 newly pressed, +8 let go (mod/src/logic.c NM_PAD_STATE).
func_80005818.name: update_controller_state

func_80005BD8.about: Sets the wanted controller mask (0x80063539) that update_controller_state copies into the active mask 0x80063538 (init_controllers' osContInit bit pattern). Callers run_match (the match, 0xF: all four) and start_front_end (the front end starting). (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: the one byte store.)
func_80005BD8.name: set_active_controllers

func_80005BE4.about: Waits for the one-message queue at 0x80063368 and marks it taken (0x8006353A = 1); returns the queue. A lock shared by the save code and open_transfer_pak (func_80005034); what it guards isn't established. (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: osRecvMesg(0x80063368, 0, blocking), 0x8006353A = 1, the queue returned; callers open_transfer_pak and take_save_lock.)
func_80005BE4.name: take_shared_lock

func_80005C28.about: Gives back the controller lock take_shared_lock took: starts a controller status query on its queue 0x80063368 (func_80034590, libultra osContStartQuery as mod/recomp/hooks_recomp.c names it; its answer is the message the next take_shared_lock waits for) and marks it free (0x8006353A = 0). So the 'lock' is the controller queue's one message: whoever takes it waits for the controllers' last request to finish. Callers the save code (release_save_lock), close_transfer_pak and init_controllers. (2026-11-12, names2: the call read from the mod's hooks; it was 'sends the message back'.)
func_80005C28.name: release_shared_lock

func_80005C54.about: Checks for a Rumble Pak on `channel`: when the controller is there (0x80063538) and has a pak in (status 0x80063388 + 4n, bit 4) and func_800399D4 (taken to be osMotorInit, pfs 0x80063398 + n x 0x68) succeeds, marks it in 0x8006353B (stopping a newly found one, stop_rumble); else clears the mark. Callers init_controllers, update_controller_state.
func_80005C54.name: init_rumble_pak

func_80005D34.about: Asks the Rumble Pak on `channel` to run: its state byte (0x8006353C + n) from 0 to 1. (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: update_rumble (confirmed) calls it for a rumble pulse's on frames and stop_rumble (confirmed, the same state byte 1 back to 0) for the off frames).
func_80005D34.name: start_rumble

func_80005D64.about: Stops `channel`'s rumble when it runs: state (0x8006353C + n) 1 to 0 and 0x80063544 + n to -1. Callers update_controller_state, init_rumble_pak, clear_rumble_queue (func_800182C0), update_rumble (func_80018338).
func_80005D64.name: stop_rumble

func_80005DA4.about: For all 4 channels: rumble state (0x8006353C) 0, 0x80063540 = `value`, 0x80063544 = -1. 4 callers.
func_80005DA4.name: reset_all_rumble

func_80005DE8.about: Calls the Controller Pak file functions (pfs_allocate_file (func_80039C20) allocate, pfs_delete_file (func_8003A050) delete, pfs_file_state (func_8003A6B0), pfs_find_file, pfs_free_blocks (func_8003ACF0), pfs_init_pak, pfs_num_files, pfs_repair_id (func_8003B1D0), func_8003A270 read-write) and voice_init (func_8002F470) all with zeros; never called. Presumably there to make the linker keep them. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_80005DE8.name: keep_pak_functions_linked

func_80005EC0.about: The game's moveset packer: turns a moveset into the packed form the roster keeps (0xD8 bytes), the reverse of unpack_moveset (func_80005EFC). The mod packs its new Superstars' movesets with it (mod/gen/mkroster.py).
func_80005EC0.name: pack_moveset

func_80005F50.about: Bit writer: ORs the low `count` bits of the 64-bit `value` (`value_hi`:`value_lo`) into `buffer`, most significant first, at the writer's place (byte 0x80063550, bit 0x80063552), which moves on; with `go` 0 instead resets the place to the start. Returns the bytes used so far. The packing counterpart of read_bits_msb_first; callers pack_ability_fields (0x37 fields), pack_moveset_slots.
func_80005F50.name: write_bits_msb_first

func_80006154.about: Bit reader: reads the next `count` bits of `buffer`, most significant first, from the reader's place (byte 0x80063554, bit 0x80063556), which moves on; returns them as a 64-bit value (v0 / v1). With `go` 0 resets the place to the start. Callers read_ability_fields (50 fields), unpack_moveset_slots (func_800075DC), ovl_e unpack_slot_moveset (func_8013CBAC).
func_80006154.name: read_bits_msb_first

func_800063BC.about: Reads the packed abilities `packed` as a run of bit fields (read_bits_msb_first (func_80006154), a bit reader, reset first; widths 3 to 6) into one byte each at `out`. Callers unpack_abilities and ovl_e read_ability_fields_from_file (func_8013CAF0) / unpack_moveset_entry (func_8013CB38). (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: read_bits_msb_first(0, 0, 0) resets the reader, then one read_bits_msb_first(packed, width, 1) per byte of `out` in order, widths 3-6.)
func_800063BC.name: read_ability_fields

func_800067CC.about: pack_moveset's first half: packs the moves `moves` into the 0xB8 bytes at `packed` (cleared first) as bit fields through write_bits_msb_first (reset first), slot by slot along the list 0x800442DC[*`kind`] (kind 0 or 1; -1 ends) with each slot's move range checks (0x800443F8) and choice tables (0x80045500, widths 0x800442E4 + 5). Unpacked again by unpack_moveset_slots (func_800075DC). (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: the 0xB8 bytes zeroed, the slot list 0x800442DC[kind < 2 ? kind : 0], write_bits_msb_first reset, then six bytes a move entry along the list until -1.)
func_800067CC.name: pack_moveset_slots

func_80006B40.about: Packs a moveset's ability fields `fields` (s16 each, 0x37 kinds through its jump table) into the 0x20 bytes at `out` (cleared first) with write_bits_msb_first; the second half of pack_moveset, the counterpart of read_ability_fields. (Corrected by the naming track, 2026-11-10; earlier named pack_ability_fields.) (2026-11-14, fablenames2 continuation: the 0x40-byte record the fields are staged in on the stack (frame +0x18) is named by offset, staged_byte_N / staged_half_N / staged_word_34: each is one value taken from `out` before the bits are packed, and which ability each one is was not worked out. ability_bits is the word at +0x34, built by or-ing the table 0x80045728's entries.)
func_80006B40.name: pack_ability_fields

func_800075DC.about: The reverse of pack_moveset_slots, called from the moveset unpacker unpack_moveset (func_80005EFC): reads the packed moves `packed` with read_bits_msb_first (reset first) along the slot list 0x800442DC[*`kind`] into `moves` (6 bytes a slot, cleared first, 0x124 entries). (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: the 0x124 six-byte entries cleared, read_bits_msb_first(0, 0, 0), the slot list 0x800442DC[*kind], walked until -1.)
func_800075DC.name: unpack_moveset_slots

func_800078B8.about: Unpacks a moveset's packed abilities `packed` into 0x37 s16 values at `out` (cleared first): read_ability_fields, then a case per value. Only caller unpack_moveset (mod/src/roster.c: unpacks moves, slots and abilities). (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: the 0x37 halfwords zeroed, read_ability_fields into the frame, then a switch over the 0x37 values setting each from the fields' bits.)
func_800078B8.name: unpack_abilities

func_80007E40.about: The position of byte `c` in the font's character order (the 0-ended table at 0x800457C0: space, Japanese punctuation, ASCII punctuation, '0'-'9', 'A'-'Z', 'a'-'z', ... as read from the ROM); 0 when absent. Callers font_glyph and to_wide_characters.
func_80007E40.name: character_index

func_80007E7C.about: Writes up to `max_chars` characters of `text` at `destination` as two-byte characters, each taken from the table at 0x80067C60 by its character_index, and ends the string; returns its end. No converted callers. The table is filled at run time (not in the ROM image), taken to be the Shift-JIS forms wide_character_index searches. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_80007E7C.name: to_wide_characters

func_80007F34.about: How many bytes the character at `text` takes: 2 when its first byte's high nibble is 0x8, 0x9, 0xE or 0xF (a two-byte Shift-JIS style character), else 1.
func_80007F34.name: character_size

func_80007F80.about: The address of hex digit `value` & 15 in the string '0123456789ABCDEF' at 0x80045964 (read from the ROM). No converted callers.
func_80007F80.name: hex_digit_address

func_80007F94.about: Copies the zero-terminated string at `source` to `destination`, the terminator included (strcpy; mod/src/gamefn.h).
func_80007F94.name: copy_string

func_80007FB8.about: Copies `source` onto the end of the string at `destination` (copy_string at its terminator), strcat-like; returns where it was appended. No converted callers.
func_80007FB8.name: append_string

func_80007FF8.about: Returns the start of the next line of `text`: steps through it character by character (character_size, so two-byte characters count whole) to the first line break (0x0A) and returns the byte after it, or the string's end (its 0) when there is none. (2026-11-12, names2: the stopping rule read from the lifted C++.)
func_80007FF8.name: skip_text_line

func_8000805C.about: The number of lines in the string `text`: 1 plus its newlines, stepping a character at a time (character_size). Callers draw_choice_lines, draw_story_text_box, draw_story_panels.
func_8000805C.name: count_text_lines

func_800080B8.about: Writes at `destination` the '#' escapes that add up to `pixels` of space ('#' then a digit or letter, 0-9 then A-Z for 10-35, at most 35 each; measure_text_lines reads '#' + digit as a width), ends the string and returns its end. Callers func_80112CB0, format_signed_number_padded.
func_800080B8.name: write_space_escapes

func_80008110.about: Finds the make_text_texture record (0x28 records of 0x58 at *0x8009EDD8; the string at +0, the key at +0x50 / +0x54) whose key is (`text`, `style`); when none, the first free one (+0x50 = 0); NULL when all are taken. Only caller make_text_texture.
func_80008110.name: find_text_record

func_80008184.about: The text texture record for (`text`, `style`): 0 when either is 0 or no record is free; otherwise the one find_text_record gives, and when it is unused (+0x50 = 0) it is taken: +0x50 / +0x54 = text / style, its 0x50 bytes cleared and +0 = 0xFF (to be drawn anew). free_text_texture gives it back. Callers the HUD's and the menus' number and date texts (minutes_seconds_text, date_text, ...). (2026-11-12, names2: confirmed from the lifted C++.)
func_80008184.name: make_text_texture

func_80008214.about: Marks a make_text_texture record free again: its key (+0x50, +0x54) cleared and +0 = 0xFF (new). Callers free_text_texture, release_text_texture_entry.
func_80008214.name: release_text_record

func_80008228.about: Looks the two-byte character at `c` up in the 0-ended table of two-byte characters at 0x80067C60 and returns its byte offset there, -1 when absent. Only caller wide_character_entry. Taken to be the font's table of double-byte (Japanese) characters. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_80008228.name: wide_character_index

func_80008274.about: The address of the two-byte character `c`'s entry in the table at 0x80067C60 (wide_character_index), 0 when it isn't there. No converted callers. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_80008274.name: wide_character_entry

func_800082A8.about: The game's bit packing: ORs the low `bits` bits of `value` into `buffer` at bit *`position` (bit 0 of the first byte up, little-endian across up to four bytes; the bits are expected clear), and moves *`position` on by `bits`. unpack_bits reads them back; mod/src/save.c reads the save with the same packing. (Roles confirmed 2026-11-12 from the code.)
func_800082A8.name: pack_bits

func_80008350.about: The game's bit unpacking, the reverse of pack_bits: returns the `bits`-bit value at bit *`position` of `buffer` (bit 0 of the first byte up, read from the four bytes there) and moves *`position` on by `bits` (mod/src/save.c reads the save the same way). (Roles confirmed 2026-11-12 from the code.)
func_80008350.name: unpack_bits

func_800083BC.about: Packs `count` characters of `text` into `packed` at 7 bits each ((count * 7 + 7) / 8 bytes), through the game's bit copy init_bit_cursor (func_800266D0). The save keeps names this way; the mod writes its select pages' names with it (mod/src/roster.c).
func_800083BC.name: pack_text_7bit

func_80008468.about: The reverse of pack_text_7bit: unpacks `count` 7-bit characters from `packed` into `text`, one byte each. The mod reads its select pages' names from the save with it (mod/src/roster.c).
func_80008468.name: unpack_text_7bit

func_800084E0.about: The glyph data of character `c` (its font index from character_index (func_80007E40)) in `style`: proportional fonts (0x8000) at 0x80065E60, 0x45 bytes a glyph (first and last columns at +0, +1, rows of 24 bits from +3); else 0x1E-byte glyphs at 0x80064260, or 0x80065060 with style 0x2000. Characters with no glyph get the blank at 0x800458C0 / 0x80045880. Callers character_pixel_width, draw_glyph_into_texture.
func_800084E0.name: font_glyph

func_80008594.about: The width in pixels of character `c` in `style`: proportional (0x8000) from the glyph's first and last columns (font_glyph (func_800084E0); 6 when there's none), fixed 0x18 with style 4; otherwise 8 with 0x4000, else 0xE, or the glyph's own. Callers measure_text_lines, escape_name_width (func_800088D4), func_80008EFC.
func_80008594.name: character_pixel_width

func_80008630.about:
The value of a character read as a digit: '0'-'9' are 0-9, letters of either case count on from 10 ('z' is 35).
Anything else is 0.
func_80008630.name: digit_value

func_80008694.about: For a text request (+0 the string, +0x12 style) works out its length (+0x14) and a hash (+0x18: the sum of each byte shifted left by (byte + position) & 15), stopping at a newline when style bit 0 is set; nothing for a number (bit 0x40000000). Only caller find_text_texture_entry.
func_80008694.name: hash_text_request

func_80008720.about: The Superstar a text name escape stands for (`text` at its letter; escape_name_costume gives the costume): 'P' / 'p' + digit, player n's (0x8053BCA0 + (n - 1) x 4, n & 3; '0' the current player *0x8004597C); 'C' / 'c' + digit, cast entry n of 0x800BD900 (16-bit, the low 12 bits; '0' entry 0); any other letter starts a three-digit ID read with digit_value (d0 << 8 | d1 << 4 | d2). Callers escape_name_width, draw_escape_name_into_texture (mod/NOTES.md: the names table at 0x800BD900). (2026-11-12, names3: renamed from text_name_number and confirmed from the lifted C++: the old about had only the cast case and its digit wrong.)
func_80008720.name: escape_name_superstar

func_80008824.about: The costume to use for the name a text escape stands for (`escape` at its letter): 'P' / 'p' + digit, player n's (0x8054B840 + n x 4; '0' the current player *0x8004597C); 'C' / 'c' + digit, (cast entry n of 0x800BD900 >> 12) & 3; 0 otherwise. Callers escape_name_width, draw_escape_name_into_texture.
func_80008824.name: escape_name_costume

func_800088D4.about: The width in pixels, in `style`, of the short name (superstar_short_name of escape_name_superstar and escape_name_costume) that the text escape `escape` stands for, summed with character_pixel_width. Caller func_80008EFC.
func_800088D4.name: escape_name_width

func_80008968.about: Draws the short name the text escape `escape` stands for into a text texture, glyph by glyph (draw_glyph_into_texture), from `x` rightward (leftward with style 2); returns the width drawn. Caller draw_text_into_texture.
func_80008968.name: draw_escape_name_into_texture

func_80008A58.about: The palette index for a colour letter in text: R 0xA, Y 0xB, G 0xC, B 0xD, W 0xF, K 1, P 6, C 7, O 9 (either case); H 0xB when the current colour (0x80069660) is 0xF, else the current; anything else the current colour. Caller draw_text_into_texture. The letters read as red, yellow, green, blue, white, black, pink, cyan, orange, highlight is a guess from the letters. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_80008A58.name: text_colour_index

func_80008AEC.about: Draws character `c`'s glyph (font data from font_glyph (func_800084E0): first and last columns at +0, +1, then 24-bit rows from +3) into a 4-bit text texture, in the colour 0x80069661 (doubled into both nibbles), style 2 mirrored, 4 fixed width, 0x8000 proportional. Returns 4 when there's no glyph, 6 for an empty one. Callers draw_escape_name_into_texture, draw_text_into_texture. (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: font_glyph(c, style), 4 when none; the colour byte *0x80069661 in both nibbles; the column step -1 for style 2; with 0x8000 (and not 4) the glyph's own first / last columns, 6 when the last is before the first.)
func_80008AEC.name: draw_glyph_into_texture

func_80008D50.about: The address of an entry in the table of 192-byte entries at 0x80063560.
func_80008D50.name: entry_in_table_80063560

func_80008D6C.about: Draws the icon a text's '$' escape names (`code`, digit_value: '0'-'9', then letters) into a 4-bit text texture `image` (pitch `pitch` pixels) at (`x`, `y`): 14 rows of 20 4-bit pixels from the 192-byte entry entry_in_table_80063560 gives (12 bytes a row), ORed in; returns its width, 20. With `style` bit 1 it steps leftward (the right-aligned text). Caller draw_text_into_texture.
func_80008D6C.name: draw_icon_into_texture

func_80008E9C.about: Measures text texture record `record`'s string in `style` (character_size, character_pixel_width (func_80008594) widths, digit_value for the '#' escapes, escape_name_width (func_800088D4) for names): sets its height +0xE, width +0x10, pitch +0xC and byte size +8 (pitch x height / 2), the margin 0x80069664 added. Callers build_text_texture (func_80009F6C) and text_width_plain (func_80113540). (Corrected by the naming track, 2026-11-10; earlier named measure_text_texture.)
func_80008E9C.name: measure_text_texture

func_800090CC.about: Draws text texture record `record`'s string (+0) into its 4-bit picture (+4, pitch +0xC, width +0x10) in `style`: colour from bits 8-10 (0 white 0xF, 0x100 red 0xA, 0x200 green 0xC, 0x300 blue 0xD, 0x400 yellow 0xB, 0x600 pink 6, 0x700 cyan 7, else 1) into 0x80069661 / 0x80069660; bit 1 right-aligned (from the width leftward); bit 0 stops at a line break; bit 15 lines 24 high, else 14; the margin 0x80069664. Escapes (doubled for the character itself): '#c' a gap of digit_value(c) pixels, '$c' an icon (draw_icon_into_texture), '%...' a name (draw_escape_name_into_texture), '@c' a colour (text_colour_index); other characters draw_glyph_into_texture. Caller build_text_texture.
func_800090CC.name: draw_text_into_texture

func_80009444.about: For the byte at (`x`, `y`) of a 4-bit text texture (`picture` +4 pixels, +0xE height; `row_bytes` a line) holding two pixels `pair`, says which of its empty pixels touch a drawn one above, below, left or right: 0x10 for the high (left) pixel, 1 for the low. Only caller outline_text_texture_once.
func_80009444.name: outline_neighbours

func_80009594.about: The unit written after a number for `options` & 0x8C0 (format_number's options), strings read from the ROM: 0x40 'lbs.' (0x80055B00), 0x80 '%' (0x80055B08, '%%'), 0xC0 'pts.' (0x80055B0C), 0x800 '"' (inches, 0x80055B18), 0x840 Shift-JIS 'kg' (0x80055B1C), 0x8C0 Shift-JIS 0x88CA (0x80055B14, read as the kanji for a place or rank), otherwise none (0x80055B24, empty). Formerly number_format_for_options.
func_80009594.name: number_unit_suffix

func_80009644.about: Returns 0x80055B24, the empty string: number_unit_suffix's 'no unit' case, a piece split off its switch (its only caller). Formerly number_format_default. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_80009644.name: no_unit_suffix

func_8000964C.about: Does nothing; a piece of number_format_for_options' switch.
func_8000964C.name: empty_8000964C

func_80009654.about: The largest power of ten not above `value` (1 for 0..9), but 10 for a single digit when `options` & 0x8C0 is 0x80 (a percentage, number_unit_suffix: two digits, zero-padded). Caller format_number.
func_80009654.name: highest_digit_place

func_800096D0.about: Writes the number `value` as text at `destination` and returns where the text ends (at its zero). With bit 0x200000 set a minus sign comes first and the magnitude is -value & 0x3FFFFF. By `options` & 0x8C0 (number_unit_suffix's kinds): 0x800 a height, `value` inches as feet ' inches (5'11), then '"'; 0x80 a percentage in tenths, with the '.' (0x80045974, the byte after the digit table "0123456789ABCDEF" at 0x80045964) before the last digit and at least one digit before it (highest_digit_place), then '%'; 0x880 a 'v' first; 0x40 'lbs.', 0xC0 'pts.', 0x840 'kg', 0x8C0 the kanji suffix, 0 nothing after. 14 callers. (Confirmed 2026-11-12: the digit table and the '.' read from the ROM, 0x80045964 = ROM 0x46564.)
func_800096D0.name: format_number

func_80009934.about: measure_text_lines on `text` in `style` with a 0x400-byte list of line widths on its own stack. Callers draw_text_lines_typed, draw_intro_featured_names, func_80112CB0, format_signed_number_padded.
func_80009934.name: measure_text

func_80009958.about: Measures the string `text` in `style` line by line into `widths` (`max_lines` words, zeroed first): character widths from character_pixel_width (func_80008594) (with character_size (func_80007F34) for the character's length), newlines starting a line (or, with style bit 0, only noted), and the escapes '#' + digit (digit_value, func_80008630), '$', '%' ('%%' a percent sign) and '@'. Only caller measure_text. What it returns isn't traced here. (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: zero_bytes(widths, max_lines x 4), then the walk with style bit 0 kept.)
func_80009958.name: measure_text_lines

func_80009B30.about: Slants a drawn text texture `record` (style bit 3, italic): each row of each line (24 high with `style` bit 15, else 14) is moved right by (line height - 1 - its row in the line) / 4 pixels, the top rows furthest, the gap at the left cleared; rows from the margin 0x80069664 to the height (+0xE) less the margin. The entry of the same routine as slant_text_texture (func_80009B80): it sets the bounds and jumps into the loop at 0x80009C7C, whose body is slant_text_texture (func_80009B80). Caller build_text_texture.
func_80009B30.name: slant_text_texture_lines

func_80009B80.about: Shifts the rows of a 4-bit text texture (`picture` +4 pixels, +0xE height less 0x80069664) sideways by amounts that change row by row, clearing what is left: an italic slant. Its loop bounds come in registers from its caller func_80009C7C, so the exact slant isn't read here. (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed from the lifted C++: each row of the 4-bit texture moved sideways by an amount that changes from row to row, the rest cleared).
func_80009B80.name: slant_text_texture

func_80009C94.about: Grows the drawing in a 4-bit text texture by one pixel: every empty pixel next to a drawn one (outline_neighbours) gets colour `colour`, written into `scratch`, then copied back over the picture (+4, +8 bytes). Only caller outline_text_texture.
func_80009C94.name: outline_text_texture_once

func_80009DD0.about: Outlines a text texture by `mode`: 0x10 six passes in colours 6 down to 1 (a fading glow), 0x20 two passes and 0x30 one pass in the outline colour 0x80069662 (outline_text_texture_once). Caller build_text_texture (making text textures).
func_80009DD0.name: outline_text_texture

func_80009E88.about: Finds the text texture table's entry (*0x80091C84, 0x80 x 0x1C) for string `text` in `style`: same string (+0), style (+0x12), length (+0x14) and hash (+0x18, hash_text_request); when none, the first free entry (+0 = 0) given that length and hash; NULL when full. Callers build_text_texture (making text textures), big_font_text_picture, release_text_texture, free_text_texture_for.
func_80009E88.name: find_text_texture_entry

func_80009F6C.about: Makes (or finds) the text texture for `text` in `style` and returns its record (find_text_texture_entry; NULL when the table is full or the picture can't be had): text with bit 30 set is a number (format_number into a buffer); style bits 4-5 an outline (margin 0x80069664 = 8 for 0x10, 2 for 0x20, 1 for 0x30, else 0); measures it (measure_text_texture, which sets +0xC / +0xE / +0x10 and the size +8), gives it heap memory (heap_alloc) unless the running total 0x80045978 would pass 0x7FFF, clears it, draws it (draw_text_into_texture), slants it with style bit 3 (slant_text_texture_lines) and outlines it (outline_text_texture, through a work copy). Callers set_name_box_superstar, cached_text_picture.
func_80009F6C.name: build_text_texture

func_8000A1BC.about: Gives a text texture back (its record `record`). mod/src/arcade.h plat_game_text_free.
func_8000A1BC.name: free_text_texture

func_8000A220.about: Releases a text texture table entry: when its string (+0) lies in a make_text_texture record (the block *0x8009EDD8, 0xDC0 bytes) that record is freed (release_text_record), and the entry is marked released (+0 = -1) for free_released_text_textures to free its picture. Only caller release_text_texture.
func_8000A220.name: release_text_texture_entry

func_8000A280.about: Goes through the text texture table (0x80 records of 0x1C at *0x80091C84) and frees the picture (+4) of every record marked released (+0 = -1), clearing it. Callers free_text_system and age_sprite_cache. (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: the 0x80 records walked, heap_free(+4) and both words cleared for +0 == -1.)
func_8000A280.name: free_released_text_textures

func_8000A2F8.about: Frees the picture (+4) of every one of the 0x80 text texture table entries (*0x80091C84) and clears each entry's string and picture. No converted callers.
func_8000A2F8.name: free_all_text_texture_pictures

func_8000A358.about: Frees the text texture of string `text` in `style` at once (find_text_texture_entry, then free_text_texture); returns -1, or 0 when there was no entry. Caller init_vs_card.
func_8000A358.name: free_text_texture_for

func_8000A388.about: Releases the text texture of string `text` in `style` (find_text_texture_entry, then release_text_texture_entry); returns -1, or 0 when there was no entry. Callers release_field_text, load_field_into_keyboard.
func_8000A388.name: release_text_texture

func_8000A3B8.about: Adds to the display list at *`display_list`: a call to the display list at 0x45830, then loading the 16-colour palette at 0x45860 into palette memory (tile 7 at TMEM 0x100), with the syncs it needs. The menu text and picture drawers call it first (43 callers). (2026-11-12: the name says only what the code does; that the palette is the menus' text palette is still a reading.)
func_8000A3B8.name: load_shared_palette

func_8000A4DC.about: With `load` set, reads four files into fixed buffers (0x4993 to 0x80063560, 0x4478 to 0x80064260, 0x4479 to 0x80065060, 0x4477 to 0x80065E60), allocates the 0x80 text entries of 0x1C bytes (0xE00 at *0x80091C84, which find_text_texture_entry (func_80009E88) searches) and the 0x28 text texture records of 0x58 bytes (0xDC0 at *0x8009EDD8, make_text_texture's: find_text_record), each marked unused, and clears 0x8009EDD0; with `load` 0 it only reads file 0x4477 into 0x80065E60 again (nothing is freed). Taken to be the fonts for the text drawer. Callers start_front_end, set_up_name_boxes, run_front_end_sequence_step, func_8012D2EC. (2026-11-12, names2: corrected from the lifted C++: the second table, and no free.)
func_8000A4DC.name: load_fonts

func_8000A5C4.about: Frees the text drawer's memory: free_released_text_textures, every text texture still in the table (free_text_texture), the block at *0x8009EDD8 and the table itself (*0x80091C84). Callers close_front_end, close_name_boxes; the reverse of load_fonts.
func_8000A5C4.name: free_text_system

func_8000A638.about: Counts the text texture table's 0x80 entries (*0x80091C84) that are free (+0 = 0) when `which` is 0, else those with no picture (+4 = 0). WrestleMania 2000's 0x8000B4EC is the same but for the vertex form (mod/gen/arenas_wm.py, mod/src/skel.c). Callers load_mesh, load_pose_mesh, load_morph_shapes. func_80027954.about: Sets the pitch offset +0x30 of every channel playing sound `handle` to `semitones` plus its fine tune +0x90 (script_set_fine_tune); update_channel_pitch adds it to the note. Returns how many. No converted callers.
