func_800279C4.about: Sets the tempo of every channel playing sound `handle`: +0x98 = `scale` held to 1..256 (128 normal) and the per-frame clock step +0x9C = base tempo +0xA8 x scale >> 7 (the frame update adds +0x9C to the clock +0xC). Returns how many. No converted callers.
func_800279C4.name: set_sound_tempo

func_80027A50.about: Sets the base effects (reverb) send +0xCB of every channel playing sound `handle` to `amount` held to 0..127, with +0xCC (the last script send applied) = 0xFF so it is sent again; returns how many. At each note the interpreter sends +0xCB + (0x80 - +0xCB) x +0xCA >> 7 (+0xCA from sound-script command 0xA2) through n_al_syn_set_fx_mix. Was named set_sound_pan (a guess); callers play_wrestler_sound (move sounds) and the menus.
func_80027A50.name: set_sound_reverb_send

func_80027AD8.about: relocate_sample_bank(`bank`, `wave_data`) and makes it the default bank (*0x8008D2AC) when there is none. Callers start_sound_system / init_audio (func_80003420) and init_sound_driver (func_80026F60) (the sound player's start). (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: the one call and the default-bank store when *0x8008D2AC is 0.)
func_80027AD8.name: set_up_sample_bank

func_80027B14.about: Makes `bank` the sample bank in use (*0x8008D2A8) when it is relocated (+0x10 negative, relocate_sample_bank's mark), and returns the one in use. No converted callers. (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: 0x8008D2A8 is fields.json's _variables wave_data_now (the sample bank in use, which start_sound_effect sets the same way)).
func_80027B14.name: set_current_wave_data

func_80027B3C.about: Makes `bank` the default sample bank (*0x8008D2AC, set_up_sample_bank's) when it is relocated (+0x10 negative). No converted callers.
func_80027B3C.name: set_default_sample_bank

func_80027B60.about: Returns the default sample bank *0x8008D2AC. No converted callers.
func_80027B60.name: default_sample_bank

func_80027B6C.about: Returns the wave data (+0x7C) of the first channel playing sound `handle`, or 0. No converted callers.
func_80027B6C.name: sound_wave_data

func_80027BC8.about: Queues sound command 0 with `handle` (queue_sound_command): run_sound_command (confirmed) sets bit 0 of the flags of the channels playing that handle, and sound_player_tick (confirmed) steps a channel's clock and script only while that bit is clear, so the sound holds where it is; command 1 (queue_sound_start) clears the bit again, and start_song starts its channels with it set. No converted callers. (2026-11-13, names5: renamed from queue_sound_stop and confirmed from the lifted C++: command 0 holds the handle's channels (flags bit 0, which the player tests before stepping them), it does not stop them).
func_80027BC8.name: queue_sound_pause

func_80027BEC.about: Queues sound command 1 with `handle` (queue_sound_command; the 8-byte command {kind 1, handle}), taken to start what start_song set up. Callers play_song, play_song_from_mark (func_80027244). (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: the two words {1, handle} on the stack handed to queue_sound_command.)
func_80027BEC.name: queue_sound_start

func_80027C14.about: Queues sound command 2 with `preset`, remembering it at *0x8008D2B4; the command handler (run_sound_command, func_80027EB8) calls select_reverb_preset. No converted callers. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: command 2 with the preset, kept at *0x8008D2B4).
func_80027C14.name: queue_reverb_change

func_80027C44.about: Sets *0x8008D2B0, which lets sound scripts change the reverb (script_select_reverb acts only when it is 1); turning it off (0) first queues the remembered preset *0x8008D2B4 back (sound command 2, queue_sound_command), and keeps the old setting when that fails. No converted callers. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_80027C44.name: set_script_reverb_control

func_80027CA0.about: Once (+0xC bit 0): turns sound effect bank `bank`'s offsets into pointers (+0x14, and each of its +0 entries' +0x18, 8 bytes apart), clears +0x10, and makes it the default bank for sounds (*0x8008D2B8, set_next_sound_bank's default) when there is none. Callers start_sound_system, init_sound_driver.
func_80027CA0.name: set_up_sound_effect_bank

func_80027D24.about: Returns word +4 of `bank` (the track or entry count, as start_song reads +4). No converted callers.
func_80027D24.name: bank_entry_count

func_80027D2C.about: Sets the default sound effect bank *0x8008D2B8 (start_sound_effect's) to `bank`. No converted callers.
func_80027D2C.name: set_default_sound_bank

func_80027D38.about: Sets the sound bank the next sound plays from (*0x8008D2BC). The game plays a sound with its bank as set_next_sound_bank then start_sound_from_bank (mod/src/media.c).
func_80027D38.name: set_next_sound_bank

func_80027D44.about: Returns the default sound effect bank *0x8008D2B8. No converted callers.
func_80027D44.name: default_sound_bank

func_80027D50.about: Stores `wave_data` at +0x10 of sound effect bank `bank` (the sample bank start_sound_effect hands on, *0x8008D2A8). Caller start_sound_system (the sound start-up, after set_up_sound_effect_bank). (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: bank_wave_data (confirmed) returns the same word +0x10 of a sound effect bank as its wave data).
func_80027D50.name: set_bank_wave_data

func_80027D58.about: Returns sound effect bank `bank`'s wave data (+0x10, set_bank_wave_data). No converted callers.
func_80027D58.name: bank_wave_data

func_80027D60.about: Sets the audio manager's scheduler hooks pointer *0x8005314C (read by create_audio_manager's code), which by default points at 0x80053140: {audio_add_scheduler_client (func_8002B2DC) register with the scheduler, wait_for_audio_retrace (func_8002B340) wait for a retrace, run_audio_task (func_8002B3A0) run an audio task}. No converted callers. (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: the default table at 0x80053140 holds the three hooks named and confirmed (audio_add_scheduler_client, wait_for_audio_retrace, run_audio_task)).
func_80027D60.name: set_audio_scheduler_hooks

func_80027D6C.about: For the first channel playing sound `handle`: word +8 of its song (+0x74) or, without one, its bank (+0x78); 0 when none. What the word is is not known. No converted callers. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_80027D6C.name: sound_source_word_8

func_80027DD0.about: For the first channel playing sound `handle`: its song's instrument table (+0x20) or, without a song, its bank's sound table (+0x14), the tables the interpreter maps +0xAE through; 0 when none. No converted callers.
func_80027DD0.name: sound_instrument_table

func_80027E48.about: Sets *0x8008D2C0, the function sound-script command 0xAB (script_sound_event, func_8002A5A4) calls with the sound's handle and a byte from the script, for sound effect channels (flags & 3 == 2). No converted callers.
func_80027E48.name: set_sound_event_callback

func_80027E54.about: Makes the ring of 8-byte sound commands (queue_sound_command) for `count` entries, held to 64..1024: the block from audio_alloc at *0x8008D2D0, size 0x8008D2CC, write and read positions 0x8008D2C8 / 0x8008D2C4 to 0. Caller init_sound_driver.
func_80027E54.name: allocate_sound_command_ring

func_80027EB8.about: Carries out one queued sound command `command`: kind +0 = 0 sets bit 0 of the flags of the channels playing handle +4 (change_sound_flags(handle, -2, 1)), 1 clears it, 2 switches the reverb preset (select_reverb_preset(+4)). Caller sound_player_tick. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_80027EB8.name: run_sound_command

func_80027F38.about: Puts the 8-byte command at `command` into the ring of commands (*0x8008D2D0, size 0x8008D2CC, write position 0x8008D2C8, read position 0x8008D2C4) with move_bytes (func_8002B80C) (a copy), returning 1, or 0 when the ring is full. Callers queue_sound_pause, queue_sound_start, queue_reverb_change, set_script_reverb_control, by the 0x8008D2xx globals the sound player's; that it feeds the sound thread is a guess.
func_80027F38.name: queue_sound_command

func_80027FD0.about: The sound driver's player handler (init_sound_driver puts it in the player at 0x8008D270 for the synthesizer to call): runs the queued sound commands (the ring 0x8008D2D0, read 0x8008D2C4 up to 0x8008D2C8, size 0x8008D2CC: run_sound_command), then steps every channel (0x8008D28C, *0x8008D284 of them): starts voices (start_channel_voice), runs their scripts and levels (run_channel_script (func_800282C0), channel_level_track_step).
func_80027FD0.name: sound_player_tick

func_800282C0.about: Sound channel `channel`'s script interpreter (the channel player sound_player_tick calls when the channel's next event is due): runs the script at +4 a command at a time (bytes >= 0x80 through the handler table 0x80052E74, each returning where to carry on; 0 ends it) up to the next note; reads the note (0x60 a rest), its optional level byte (+0xD2 / +0xD3 into +0xBB) and its length (one or two bytes, unless the fixed length +0xAC) into +0x9A, moves the note times (+0x40 start, +0x3C end); for a note looks up the drum or instrument map (+0x84 / the song's tables) for its sample, pan and envelope, starts the envelope (start_channel_envelope), the pan sweep (reset_channel_auto_pan) and the voice `voice` (start_channel_voice, or only its volume, n_al_syn_set_vol, when legato), works out the pitch +0x2C (note + transpose) and sends a changed effects mix (n_al_syn_set_fx_mix). Caller sound_player_tick. The rest-path's details are not traced. (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: command bytes >= 0x80 go through the handler table (the converted code's lift_pointer call), each returning the next script place, 0 ending it; the place is written back to the channel's script.)
func_800282C0.name: run_channel_script

func_8002880C.about: Starts sound channel `channel`'s voice `index` (*0x8008D288 + index x 0x1C, an ALVoice) on the channel's wave table (+8, then cleared), stopping it first (n_al_syn_stop_voice) when the channel's playing flag (+0xC9) is set, and sets that flag. Callers sound_player_tick, run_channel_script (the channel players).
func_8002880C.name: start_channel_voice

func_80028888.about: Gives sound channel `channel`'s voice `index` its volume: the product of +0xBC, +0xC4, +0xBB and the volume +0x9E (>> 13), scaled by the master level for its group (0x8008D29C or 0x8008D29E, set_sound_levels), over *0x8008D298 (n_al_syn_set_vol); and its pan +0xBD, centred when mono (0x80052E70, set_mono_sound) (n_al_syn_set_pan). Caller sound_player_tick. (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: the volume is the product of fields.json's SoundChannel level, envelope_level, velocity and volume, and the pan is the channel's pan x pan_scale).
func_80028888.name: apply_channel_volume_and_pan

func_800289F0.about: Sound channel `channel`'s pitch for voice `index`: its note (+0x2C), glided from +0x4C over +0xB8 frames when set (+0xAA the frames played; the current kept at +0x50), plus `pitch_offset` and +0x24; when it changed from +0x28, times 0x80055E80 (a semitone in octaves, by use) through power_of_two to n_al_syn_set_pitch. Caller sound_player_tick. (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: +0xB8 is the glide time of script_set_glide (confirmed); the pitch goes to the voice through n_al_syn_set_pitch).
func_800289F0.name: update_channel_pitch

func_80028AFC.about: Starts sound channel `channel`'s envelope for a new note (the interpreter calls it unless +0xD6 is set): its release time +0x54 is the note start +0x40 plus the hold time +0xB2, or the note end +0x3C less the release gap +0xB4, or never for length 0x7FFF; stage +0xC3 = 1, level +0xC4 = the start level +0xC0, counter +0xC5 = +0xBF.
func_80028AFC.name: start_channel_envelope

func_80028B6C.about: Sound channel `channel`'s envelope for this frame into the level +0xC4: at the release time (+0x54 passed by the clock +0xC) goes to stage 4 from the level then (+0xCD); stage 1 ramps +0xC0 to +0xC1 over +0xC6, stage 2 +0xC1 to +0xC2 over +0xC7, 3 holds, 4 falls to 0 over +0xC8, then 5 (time in ticks scaled by +0x64). Caller sound_player_tick, the sound player's frame update.
func_80028B6C.name: channel_envelope_step

func_80028D48.about: Restarts sound channel `channel`'s pan sweep: +0xD9 (fraction) 0, +0x94 from +0x40, direction (+0xDA) from bit 0x40 of the pan +0xBD. Caller run_channel_script. (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: run_channel_script calls it at each note while the auto-pan speed (+0xD4, fields.json auto_pan_speed) is not 0; it restarts the sweep's fraction, start and direction).
func_80028D48.name: reset_channel_auto_pan

func_80028D64.about: Moves sound channel `channel`'s pan (+0xBD) by its sweep speed (+0xD4, in 1/64 steps through +0xD9), up to 0x7F then back down (+0xDA the direction), and advances +0x94 by 0x100. Caller sound_player_tick. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_80028D64.name: channel_auto_pan_step

func_80028E1C.about: Counts sound channel `channel`'s gate timer (+0xD0) down and at 0 flips its state (+0xD1) between off (for +0xCF frames) and +0xD8 (for +0xCE frames); returns the state as a float. Caller sound_player_tick. (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: the channel player func_80027FD0 calls it only while the gate's on frames (+0xCE) are not 0 and adds its result to the note's pitch, so the gate switches the pitch between +0 and +0xD8 semitones: a trill).
func_80028E1C.name: channel_gate_step

func_80028E74.about: Sound channel `channel`'s vibrato for this frame: 0 until +0xB6 frames have played (+0xAA), then sine((frames - delay) x rate +0xDC) x depth +0x20, kept at +0x68. Caller sound_player_tick. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_80028E74.name: channel_vibrato

func_80028ED8.about: Steps sound channel `channel`'s level track (+0x38) up to the clock +0xC, 0x100 per tick at +0x14: each entry a byte < 0x80 (the level +0xBC for one tick) or the level | 0x80 followed by a length (1 or 2 bytes, + 2), counted in +0xA2. Caller sound_player_tick.
func_80028ED8.name: channel_level_track_step

func_80028F9C.about: Steps sound channel `channel`'s pitch bend track (+0x34) up to the clock +0xC, 0x100 per tick at +0x18: each entry a value (the low 7 bits) less 64 (0x80055E90) to +0x70, times the bend range +0x6C into the bend +0x24 (update_channel_pitch adds it), lasting one tick or the length after it (+0xA4). Caller sound_player_tick.
func_80028F9C.name: channel_bend_track_step

func_800290B0.about: 2 to the power `x`: 1 for 0; for x > 0 a series in x with ln 2 terms (constants at 0x80055ED0.. ; 0x80055E98 = ln 2 = 0.693147), for x < 0 one over the same series in -x. Only caller update_channel_pitch (an octave count to a pitch ratio).
func_800290B0.name: power_of_two

func_80029244.about: Once per bank (+0x10 bit 31 marks it done): turns the bank's offset tables at +0x24 and +0x2C into pointers (add_to_nonzero_words), makes each of its +0x20 instruments' tuning a float (signed byte / 0x80055F08 plus the +0x24 byte - 0x30, a fine and coarse tune by the look), and points each instrument's sample (+0 unless 0xFF......) into the wave data `wave_data` (+9 marks it done) and its +0xC within the bank. Only caller set_up_sample_bank. (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed from the lifted C++: the bank's offset tables become pointers (add_to_nonzero_words with the bank's address) once, marked by bit 31 of +0x10).
func_80029244.name: relocate_sample_bank

func_800293DC.about: The sound scripts' random number for `range`: steps the sound player's 32-bit shift register *0x8008D2A4 eight times (shift left, shifting in a 1 when bit 27 was set: the test compares the bits 0x48000000 with both 0x48000000 and 0x08000000, so bit 30 makes no difference) and returns `range` x register / 2^32, truncated. The register is read as a signed number, so the result runs from about -range / 2 to range / 2, not 0..range as the callers' abouts say ('below the first byte'). Callers script_random_transpose, script_random_level, script_random_pan.
func_800293DC.name: sound_script_random

func_80029470.about: Resets sound channel record `channel` (0x13C bytes, the channels at *0x8008D28C) for a new sound, keeping its byte +0xC9: all zero, then the defaults (+0xBC / +0xC1 / +0xC2 / +0xD3 = 0x7F, +0xBD 0x40, +0xBE / +0xCC / +0xC7 0xFF, +0xBF / +0xC6 1, +0xC8 0xF, +0x9E / +0xB0 / +0x98 0x80, +0xA0 -1, +0x10 -1, floats +0x28 99.9, +0x58 1, +0x5C 1/255, +0x60 1/15, +0x6C 1/32), +0x9C / +0xA8 = 0x6000 / the output rate *0x8008D294, +0x7C the wave data *0x8008D2A8 (else *0x8008D2AC). Callers restart_sound_on_channel, start_sound_on_free_channel, start_song, init_sound_driver (func_80026F60).
func_80029470.name: reset_sound_channel

func_800295AC.about: Picks a sound channel for song `song`'s track `track` (start_song): a negative `track` (the song's master) takes the first free channel (+4 == 0) of 0-3; a track takes the first free one from 4 up, else the playing channel with the lowest priority (+0x48) whose song (+0x74) is not this one and that is not a master (+0x78), else falls back further; returns its index.
func_800295AC.name: find_channel_for_track

func_80029774.about: Adds an amount to each word of a list that isn't zero. It looks like it's turning offsets in a loaded file into addresses, with zero meaning "nothing here". (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_80029774.name: add_to_nonzero_words

func_800297AC.about: Restarts sound channel `channel` with sound `sound` of bank `bank`: reset (reset_sound_channel, func_80029470), sound +0xA6, bank +0x78, `volume` +0x9E, `pan` +0xB0, a new handle +0x44 (counter *0x8008D2A0), `priority` +0x48, the bank's wave data (+0x10) at +0x7C when set, and the script (bank entry +0x18) at +0x80 and +4. Returns the handle. Only caller start_sound_effect (its reuse case).
func_800297AC.name: restart_sound_on_channel

func_8002985C.about: Starts sound `sound` of bank `bank` on the first free sound channel from 4 up (+4, the script, 0): resets it (reset_sound_channel, func_80029470) and sets the sound (+0xA6), bank (+0x78), `volume` (+0x9E), pan, priority (`priority`, -1 = the bank entry's +0x1C), a new handle (+0x44, from the counter *0x8008D2A0) and the script from the bank entry. Returns the handle. Callers start_sound_from_bank, start_sound_effect, script_start_sub_sound (func_8002A444). (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: priority -1 takes bank + sound x 8 + 0x1C; the channels from 4 to *0x8008D284 in *0x8008D290, the first with +4 == 0 reset (reset_sound_channel) and given sound +0xA6, bank +0x78, volume +0x9E, pan +0xB0, priority +0x48, handle +0x44 = *0x8008D2A0 (then counted up).)
func_8002985C.name: start_sound_on_free_channel

func_80029A04.about: Starts song data `song` on the sound channels (0x8008D28C, 0x13C each): on first use (+0x28 = 0) turns its seven offset words from +0xC and the track tables at +0xC / +0x10 / +0x14 (count +4) into pointers; takes a master channel (flags | 3, +0x74 the song, +0x80 / +4 from +0x24) and one channel per track with a script (find_channel_for_track (func_800295AC) finds it, reset_sound_channel (func_80029470) resets it; +0x80 / +4 the track's script, +0x8C / +0x38 and +0x88 / +0x34 from the other two tables), all with the new handle at +0x44. Returns the handle. Callers play_song, play_song_from_mark (func_80027244). (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: on first use (+0x28 0, then 1) the seven words from +0xC made song-relative pointers, then the +4 track entries of the table at +0xC likewise.)
func_80029A04.name: start_song

func_80029C70.about: For every sound channel (0x8008D28C, 0x13C each, count *0x8008D284) playing `handle` (+0x44): flags (+0) = flags & `keep` | `set`. Caller run_sound_command (the sound command handler, by the look).
func_80029C70.name: change_sound_flags

func_80029CC4.about: Sets the mono flag 0x80052E70: while it is set apply_channel_volume_and_pan (func_80028888) gives every voice the centre pan (0x40) instead of its own. Only caller set_stereo.
func_80029CC4.name: set_mono_sound

func_80029CD0.about: Sound-script command 0x80 (entry 0 of the command table at 0x80052E74, which the channel script interpreter run_channel_script (func_800282C0) calls for every script byte >= 0x80 with the channel and the script after the opcode, carrying on from what the handler returns): clears the channel's level and bend tracks (+0x38, +0x34), song (+0x74), bank (+0x78), handle (+0x44) and wave table (+8) and returns 0, which ends the script.
func_80029CD0.name: script_end

func_80029CF0.about: Sound-script command 0x81: reads a number (one byte, or two when the first has bit 7: 15 bits) into +0xAE, the instrument; the interpreter turns +0xAE into a sample through the song's table +0x20 (or the bank's +0x14), 0xFFFF there making the note a rest.
func_80029CF0.name: script_set_instrument

func_80029D20.about: Sound-script command 0x82: reads the glide (portamento) time +0xB8 in frames, and when it is set starts the glide from the current note (+0x50 = +0x2C); update_channel_pitch glides from +0x4C over +0xB8 frames. Command 0x83 (script_glide_off) turns it off.
func_80029D20.name: script_set_glide

func_80029D40.about: A sound-script command, by its shape: sets 0xB8 bytes into the channel to 0, and carries on from the same place in the script. (Renamed from script_set_B8_to_0 by the naming track, 2026-11-10.) (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: +0xB8 is the glide time script_set_glide (confirmed) sets and update_channel_pitch glides over only while it is not 0).
func_80029D40.name: script_glide_off

func_80029D4C.about: Sound-script command 0x84: reads a 7-byte envelope into the channel: +0xBF time scale (+0x64 = 1024 / it), +0xC0 start level, +0xC6 frames to +0xC1 (rate +0x58), +0xC7 frames to +0xC2 (rate +0x5C), +0xC8 release frames (+0x60 = 1 / it); channel_envelope_step runs it. Same layout as a song envelope (script_use_song_envelope).
func_80029D4C.name: script_set_envelope

func_80029E74.about: Sound script command 0x85, the song tempo (the handler table 0x80052E74, entry 5, holds 0x80029E74): `data` byte 0 (beats a minute) -> ticks a frame = byte x 0x6000 / 120 / the frame rate *0x8008D294; on a master channel (+0x78 set) only its +0x9C, otherwise every channel of the song (+0x74 the same) gets +0xA8 (base tempo) = that and +0x9C (clock step) = that x its tempo scale +0x98 >> 7. Called only through the table by the script interpreter run_channel_script (func_800282C0).
func_80029E74.name: set_song_tempo

func_80029F58.about: Sound-script command 0x87: +0xB4 = the next byte and +0xB2 = 0: start_channel_envelope then releases each note +0xB4 ticks before it ends (rather than a fixed hold time +0xB2, script_set_hold_time). (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: +0xB4 / +0xB2 are fields.json's SoundChannel release_gap / hold_time).
func_80029F58.name: script_set_release_gap

func_80029F6C.about: Sound-script command 0x86: +0xB2 = the next two bytes (big-endian) and +0xB4 = 0: start_channel_envelope then releases each note a fixed +0xB2 ticks after it starts. (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: +0xB2 / +0xB4 are fields.json's SoundChannel hold_time / release_gap).
func_80029F6C.name: script_set_hold_time

func_80029F90.about: Sound-script command 0x88, three bytes: delay +0xB6 (frames), period +0xD5 (rate +0xDC = 2 pi / period, 0x80055F20) and depth +0x20 = byte / 50 (0x80055F18); channel_vibrato reads exactly these.
func_80029F90.name: script_set_vibrato

func_8002A000.about: Sound-script command 0x89: as script_set_vibrato (0x88) but the depth is negated (+0x20 = -byte / 50), so the vibrato starts downwards.
func_8002A000.name: script_set_inverted_vibrato

func_8002A074.about: Sound-script command 0x8A: clears the vibrato period +0xD5 and its current value +0x68 (channel_vibrato's), so no vibrato.
func_8002A074.name: script_vibrato_off

func_8002A084.about: Sound-script command 0x8B: reads a number (one byte, or 15 bits over two when bit 7 is set) into +0xAC, a fixed length for the following notes: while it is set the interpreter takes each note's length (+0x9A) from it instead of the script (0x8C, script_next_note_has_length, makes the next note read its own). 0xAC (script_note_length_off) clears it.
func_8002A084.name: script_set_note_length

func_8002A0B4.about: A sound-script command, by its shape: sets 0xB7 bytes into the channel to 1, and carries on from the same place in the script. (Renamed from script_set_B7_to_1 by the naming track, 2026-11-10.) (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: run_channel_script, while a fixed length (+0xAC) is set and +0xB7 is not 0, clears +0xB7 and reads the next note's length from the script).
func_8002A0B4.name: script_next_note_has_length

func_8002A0C4.about: A sound-script command, by its shape: reads one byte of the script into 0xB9 bytes into the channel, and carries on after it. (Renamed from script_read_B9 by the naming track, 2026-11-10.) (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: +0xB9 is fields.json's SoundChannel transpose).
func_8002A0C4.name: script_set_transpose

func_8002A0D4.about: Sound-script command 0x8E: sets +0xBA; the interpreter adds the transpose +0xB9 to each note times (1 - +0xBA), so this switches the transpose off.
func_8002A0D4.name: script_ignore_transpose

func_8002A0E4.about: Sound-script command 0x8F: a signed byte in cents: +0x90 = byte / 100 semitones (0x80055F38 = 100.0), with the pitch offset +0x30 moved by the change (minus the old +0x90, plus the new).
func_8002A0E4.name: script_set_fine_tune

func_8002A13C.about: A sound-script command, by its shape: sets 0xD6 bytes into the channel to 1, and carries on from the same place in the script. (Renamed from script_set_D6_to_1 by the naming track, 2026-11-10.) (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: while +0xD6 is not 0, run_channel_script does not call start_channel_envelope at the next note, so the envelope carries on (held) from note to note).
func_8002A13C.name: script_envelope_hold_on

func_8002A14C.about: A sound-script command, by its shape: sets 0xD6 bytes into the channel to 0, and carries on from the same place in the script. (Renamed from script_set_D6_to_0 by the naming track, 2026-11-10.) (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: +0xD6 back to 0 makes run_channel_script call start_channel_envelope at each note again (see script_envelope_hold_on)).
func_8002A14C.name: script_envelope_hold_off

func_8002A158.about: A sound-script command, by its shape: sets 0xD7 bytes into the channel to 1, and carries on from the same place in the script. (Renamed from script_set_D7_to_1 by the naming track, 2026-11-10.) (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: +0xD7 is fields.json's SoundChannel tie (don't restart the sample), which run_channel_script tests before starting the note's sample).
func_8002A158.name: script_tie_on

func_8002A168.about: A sound-script command, by its shape: sets 0xD7 bytes into the channel to 0, and carries on from the same place in the script. (Renamed from script_set_D7_to_0 by the naming track, 2026-11-10.) (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: +0xD7 is fields.json's SoundChannel tie (don't restart the sample), which run_channel_script tests before starting the note's sample).
func_8002A168.name: script_tie_off

func_8002A174.about: Sound-script command 0x95: pushes a loop at depth +0xDB (then +1): its repeat count (the next byte, 0xFF for ever) at +0x120, the script position after it at +0xE0, and the level and bend tracks' state (+0x38 to +0xF0, +0x34 to +0x100, +0xBC to +0x124, +0x70 to +0x128, +0xA2 to +0x110, +0xA4 to +0x118). script_loop_end goes back to it.
func_8002A174.name: script_loop_start

func_8002A1E0.about: Sound-script command 0x97, three bytes: the gate's on level +0xD8, on frames +0xCE and off frames +0xCF, which channel_gate_step switches between (a tremolo or stutter). 0x98 (script_gate_off) turns it off.
func_8002A1E0.name: script_set_gate

func_8002A208.about: A sound-script command, by its shape: sets 0xCE bytes into the channel to 0, and carries on from the same place in the script. (Renamed from script_set_CE_to_0 by the naming track, 2026-11-10.) (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: +0xCE is the gate's on frames (script_set_gate, confirmed), and the channel player func_80027FD0 calls channel_gate_step only while +0xCE is not 0).
func_8002A208.name: script_gate_off

func_8002A214.about: A sound-script command, by its shape: sets 0xD2 bytes into the channel to 1, and carries on from the same place in the script. (Renamed from script_set_D2_to_1 by the naming track, 2026-11-10.) (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: +0xD2 is fields.json's SoundChannel velocity_per_note, the flag that makes run_channel_script read a level byte with each note).
func_8002A214.name: script_velocity_per_note_on

func_8002A224.about: A sound-script command, by its shape: sets 0xD2 bytes into the channel to 0, and carries on from the same place in the script. (Renamed from script_set_D2_to_0 by the naming track, 2026-11-10.) (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: +0xD2 is fields.json's SoundChannel velocity_per_note, the flag that makes run_channel_script read a level byte with each note).
func_8002A224.name: script_velocity_per_note_off

func_8002A230.about: Sound-script command 0x9B: a fixed note velocity +0xD3 = the next byte, and +0xD2 = 0 so notes no longer carry their own (0x99 / 0x9A set and clear +0xD2); the interpreter copies it to +0xBB, which apply_channel_volume_and_pan multiplies in.
func_8002A230.name: script_set_velocity

func_8002A244.about: Sound-script command 0x9C: the pan +0xBD = byte / 2 (0..127), with +0xBE (the last pan sent) = 0xFF so it is sent again.
func_8002A244.name: script_set_pan

func_8002A260.about: A sound-script command, by its shape: skips 2 bytes of the script. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_8002A260.name: script_skip_2

func_8002A268.about: Sound-script command 0x9E: reads an index (8 or 15 bits) and sets +0x84 to the song's (+0x74) drum map table +0x1C + index x 6; while +0x84 is set the interpreter looks each note up there (6 bytes per note: +0 instrument, +2 song envelope, +4 pan x 2, +5 the note played). 0x9F (script_drum_map_off) clears it.
func_8002A268.name: script_set_drum_map

func_8002A2B0.about: A sound-script command, by its shape: sets 0x84 bytes into the channel to 0, and carries on from the same place in the script. (Renamed from script_set_84_to_0 by the naming track, 2026-11-10.) (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: it clears the drum map (fields.json SoundChannel +0x84 drum_map), and script_set_drum_map's confirmed note names 0x9F as the command that clears it).
func_8002A2B0.name: script_drum_map_off

func_8002A2BC.about: A sound-script command, by its shape: skips 1 byte of the script. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_8002A2BC.name: script_skip_1

func_8002A2C4.about: Sound-script command 0xA1, three big-endian 16-bit offsets: continues the script at +0x80 (the script base) + the first, restarts the level track at +0x8C + the second (+0x38, +0xA2 = 1) and the bend track at +0x88 + the third (+0x34, +0xA4 = 1).
func_8002A2C4.name: script_jump_with_tracks

func_8002A334.about: A sound-script command, by its shape: reads one byte of the script into 0xCA bytes into the channel, and carries on after it. (Renamed from script_read_CA by the naming track, 2026-11-10.) (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: +0xCA is fields.json's SoundChannel script_reverb (the script's reverb amount)).
func_8002A334.name: script_set_reverb_amount

func_8002A344.about: Sound-script command 0xA3: the transpose +0xB9 = a random number below the first byte (sound_script_random (func_800293DC), the sound player's shift-register random number at *0x8008D2A4) plus the second.
func_8002A344.name: script_random_transpose

func_8002A394.about: Sound-script command 0xA4: the level +0xBC (as the level track and 0xA6, script_set_level, set it) = random below the first byte (sound_script_random, func_800293DC) plus the second.
func_8002A394.name: script_random_level

func_8002A3E4.about: Sound-script command 0xA5: the pan +0xBD = random below the first byte (sound_script_random, func_800293DC) plus the second.
func_8002A3E4.name: script_random_pan

func_8002A434.about: A sound-script command, by its shape: reads one byte of the script into 0xBC bytes into the channel, and carries on after it. (Renamed from script_read_BC by the naming track, 2026-11-10.) (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: +0xBC is fields.json's SoundChannel level).
func_8002A434.name: script_set_level

func_8002A444.about: Sound-script command 0xA7: reads a sound number (8 or 15 bits) and starts it from the channel's bank (+0x78) with its volume (+0x9E) and pan (+0xB0) through start_sound_on_free_channel, at priority +0x48 + 1; the channels of the new sound then take this sound's handle (+0x44) and wave data (+0x7C), so they stop with it.
func_8002A444.name: script_start_sub_sound

func_8002A514.about: Sound-script command 0xA8: +0x6C = byte / 64 (0x80055F40), the semitones per step of the bend track, and the bend +0x24 recomputed from its current value +0x70 (channel_bend_track_step's). (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: +0x6C / +0x70 / +0x24 are fields.json's SoundChannel bend_range / bend_value / bend).
func_8002A514.name: script_set_bend_range

func_8002A550.about: A sound-script command, by its shape: reads one byte of the script into 0xD4 bytes into the channel, and carries on after it. (Renamed from script_read_D4 by the naming track, 2026-11-10.) (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: +0xD4 is fields.json's SoundChannel auto_pan_speed, and run_channel_script calls reset_channel_auto_pan at each note only while it is not 0).
func_8002A550.name: script_set_auto_pan_speed

func_8002A560.about: Sound-script command 0xAA: select_reverb_preset(the next byte) when scripts may change the reverb (*0x8008D2B0 == 1, set_script_reverb_control).
func_8002A560.name: script_select_reverb

func_8002A5A4.about: Sound-script command 0xAB: skips its sound number (one byte, or two when the first has bit 0x80) and, for a sound effect channel (`channel` +0 & 3 == 2) with a callback set (*0x8008D2C0, set_sound_event_callback), calls it with the channel's sound handle (+0x44) and the command's first byte. Returns where the script carries on. Lets the game hear a mark placed in a sound effect. (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: the callback it calls is the one set_sound_event_callback (confirmed) keeps at 0x8008D2C0).
func_8002A5A4.name: script_sound_event

func_8002A614.about: A sound-script command, by its shape: sets 0xAC bytes into the channel to 0, and carries on from the same place in the script. (Renamed from script_set_AC_to_0 by the naming track, 2026-11-10.) (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: +0xAC is the fixed note length script_set_note_length (confirmed) reads, which the interpreter run_channel_script uses only while it is not 0).
func_8002A614.name: script_note_length_off

func_8002A620.about: Starts the second (n_audio style) audio library, whose sound system is at *0x80053414: when its globals pointer *0x80053410 is unset, sets it to `globals`, and when there is no synthesizer yet sets the configuration `config`'s effects to the custom kind (use_custom_reverb (func_8002AD70): +0x1C = 6, +0x20 = the parameters at 0x80052F98), points *0x80053414 and *0x800A9958 at the globals and makes the synthesizer (n_al_syn_new, func_8002A688). libultra n_alInit by its shape (al_init is the other library's alInit at 0x80033AA0). Only caller create_audio_manager. (Confirmed 2026-11-12: n_alInit's shape with the reverb set-up added before n_alSynNew.)
func_8002A620.name: n_al_init

func_8002A688.about: Makes the second audio library's synthesizer (*0x80053414) from configuration `config` (libultra n_alSynNew by its shape): from the configuration's heap, the 0x44-byte bus record (+0x34) with a source list for the +4 voices, a 0x14-byte record (+0x30), the effects (n_al_syn_alloc_fx bus 0), then +4 physical voices of 0x8C bytes each linked (al_link) into the free list at +4 and set up with n_al_pvoice_new (func_8002BE3C), and the parameter records. Only caller n_al_init. (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: the synth *0x80053414's player list, times and output buffer cleared, +0x44 = 0xB8 (184 samples a sub-frame), then al_heap_alloc(0, 0, heap, 1, 0x44) for the bus, as libultra n_alSynNew.)
func_8002A688.name: n_al_syn_new

func_8002A8F8.about: Makes the effects unit for bus `bus` (n_al_fx_new into the bus record's +0x24 + bus x 4, the bus record at the synthesizer's +0x34) from configuration `config` and heap `heap`, and returns it (libultra alSynAllocFX). Only caller n_al_syn_new.
func_8002A8F8.name: n_al_syn_alloc_fx

func_8002A948.about: Makes an effects (reverb) unit at `fx` from configuration `config` on heap `heap`: sizes its delay line by the largest delay values of the parameter set (largest_first_value, largest_second_value), allocates it (al_heap_alloc) and loads the parameters (load_reverb_params). libultra alFxNew by its role. Only caller n_al_syn_alloc_fx. (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed: n_al_syn_alloc_fx (confirmed, alSynAllocFX) makes the bus's effects unit with it, and n_al_fx_new_stock is the library's own copy).
func_8002A948.name: n_al_fx_new

func_8002AA90.about: Loads a reverb parameter set `params` into the effects unit (globals 0x800A9958, 0x800A9968.., float maths with init_lpfilter (func_800308F0)): section count, delays and gains. Callers n_al_fx_new, select_reverb_preset. (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: the fx record (*0x800A9958 +0x34 +0x24) takes the section count (+0x24 byte) and the delay length (+0x1C) from params +0 / +4, its buffers from 0x800A9968 / 0x800A996C, the delay line cleared, then the sections' values from params + 8 on.)
func_8002AA90.name: load_reverb_params

func_8002AD70.about: Sets the synthesizer configuration `config`'s effect type (+0x1C) to 6 (AL_FX_CUSTOM in libultra) and its parameters (+0x20) to the game's table at 0x80052F98. Only caller n_al_init. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed: AL_FX_CUSTOM is 6 in libultra (n_alInit / alSynNew read the custom parameters through +0x20)).
func_8002AD70.name: use_custom_reverb

func_8002AD88.about: Goes through the zero-ended list of pointers at 0x80053124 and returns the largest of the values they point at.
func_8002AD88.name: largest_first_value

func_8002ADCC.about: Goes through the zero-ended list of pointers at 0x80053124 and returns the largest of the values 4 bytes into what they point at.
func_8002ADCC.name: largest_second_value

func_8002AE10.about: Switches the effects to reverb preset `preset` when it is under the preset count *0x80053120: load_reverb_params(0x80053124[preset]) and al_fx_param (func_800331A4) on the effects unit (the bus record at *0x800A9958 + 0x34); returns 0, or 1 for a bad number. Callers run_sound_command (a sound command), script_select_reverb.
func_8002AE10.name: select_reverb_preset

func_8002AE70.about: Makes the audio DMA cache: `count` 0x14-byte buffer records (*0x8008D2E8, linked into the free list *0x8008D2E4; +0xC start -1, +0x10 a `size`-byte buffer from audio_alloc), DMA requests (count x 0x30, *0x8008D2EC), the message queue 0x8008D300 (count x 2 messages), the cartridge handle (*0x8008D318, osCartRomInit), the in-use list *0x8008D2E0 empty. Returns 0x8002B0B4 (audio_dma_new), the DMA set-up callback the synthesizer is given. Used by audio_dma_cache_get. Only caller create_audio_manager.
func_8002AE70.name: set_up_audio_dma

func_8002AFE4.about: Once a frame on the audio thread: takes the finished DMA messages off 0x8008D300 (*0x8008D2F8 of them) and counts each cached buffer's frames-left (+8) down, moving those at 0 from the in-use list *0x8008D2E0 to the free list *0x8008D2E4. The sample audiomgr's __clearAudioDMA. Caller func_8002B5B8 (the audio thread).
func_8002AFE4.name: clear_audio_dma

func_8002B0B4.about: The synthesizer's DMA set-up callback (set_up_audio_dma returns it): returns the DMA routine at 0x8002B0C0 (which leads to audio_dma_cache_get). The sample audiomgr's __amDmaNew. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: it returns the routine 0x8002B0C0, as the sample audio manager's __amDmaNew returns its DMA callback).
func_8002B0B4.name: audio_dma_new

func_8002B12C.about: Returns a buffer in the audio DMA cache that holds `length` bytes from ROM address `rom_address`, reading them from ROM if they aren't cached yet: the audio library's DMA callback (mod/src/arcade.h GF_AUDIO_DMA, mod/src/media.c).
func_8002B12C.name: audio_dma_cache_get

func_8002B2D0.about: Sets *0x8008D320, the scheduler the audio manager's hooks use (audio_add_scheduler_client (func_8002B2DC) adds a client to it, run_audio_task (func_8002B3A0) sends its tasks there). Caller init_sound_driver with word +8 of the sound system settings.
func_8002B2D0.name: set_audio_scheduler

func_8002B2DC.about: The audio manager's first scheduler hook (table 0x80053140, set_audio_scheduler_hooks): takes a 0x58-byte record from the audio heap (*0x8008D324): a 4-message queue at +8 (buffer +0x20) for the scheduler's messages and one at +0x30 (buffer +0x48) for finished tasks, and adds it as a client of the scheduler *0x8008D320 (scheduler_add_client with the +8 queue).
func_8002B2DC.name: audio_add_scheduler_client

func_8002B340.about: Waits on the audio manager's queue (*0x8008D324 + 8) until a message of type 1 (the retrace the audio thread is driven by) has come, emptying the queue as it goes. No converted caller. Message type 1 is libultra's OS_SC_RETRACE_MSG (sched.h); it is the middle hook of the audio manager's scheduler hook table 0x80053140 {audio_add_scheduler_client, this, run_audio_task}.
func_8002B340.name: wait_for_audio_retrace

func_8002B3A0.about: The audio manager's third scheduler hook: builds an OSScTask on the stack for audio command list `task` (+0 the list, +4 its length, +8 the microcode, +0xC its data): flags 2, an M_AUDTASK (type 2) with the RSP boot code 0x80040380 (0xD0 bytes), microcode sizes 0x1000 / 0x800, done message to the record's +0x30 queue; sends it to the scheduler's audio queue (scheduler_audio_queue) and waits for it to finish.
func_8002B3A0.name: run_audio_task

func_8002B480.about: Starts the audio manager (as the N64 sample audiomgr's amCreateAudioMgr): the synthesizer configuration on the stack from `settings` (+4 voices, +0x28, DMA buffers +0x38 x +0x3C bytes through set_up_audio_dma, output rate osAiSetFrequency(+0x2C), the audio heap), n_al_init with the globals 0x800A93C8, frame sizes (set_audio_frame_sizes(+0x34, rate, `fields`, 10)), command lists (+0x30 x 8 at *0x8008D4E8), three audio buffers (*0x8008D4E4), and the audio thread (0x8008D330, id 3, at 0x8002B5B8, an 0x2000-byte stack *0x8008D4E0, priority +0xC). Only caller init_sound_driver (the sound player's start). (2026-11-13, names5: confirmed against the N64 SDK sample audiomgr.c (amCreateAudioMgr): the synthesizer configuration on the stack, osAiSetFrequency, n_al_init, the frame sizes, the command list and audio info buffers (three), and the audio thread (osCreateThread 0x8008D330, priority from settings +0xC)).
func_8002B480.name: create_audio_manager

func_8002B740.about: Zeroes `size` bytes at `base` (fill_bytes) and makes them the audio heap 0x8008D4F0 (start_sound_heap) that audio_alloc takes from. Caller init_sound_driver.
func_8002B740.name: set_up_audio_heap

func_8002B78C.about: Takes `size` bytes from the game's audio heap (0x8008D4F0) through al_heap_alloc.
func_8002B78C.name: audio_alloc

func_8002B7BC.about: Bytes taken from the audio heap so far: its current pointer (*0x8008D4F4) less its base (*0x8008D4F0). Caller init_sound_driver.
func_8002B7BC.name: audio_heap_used

func_8002B7D4.about: Returns the audio heap record 0x8008D4F0 (base, current, length). Caller create_audio_manager (the synthesizer's heap).
func_8002B7D4.name: audio_heap

func_8002B7E0.about: Sets a run of bytes to one value: the C library function memset, without its return value.
func_8002B7E0.name: fill_bytes

func_8002B80C.about: Copies `length` bytes from `source` to `destination` a byte at a time, from the end when the source is below the destination, so overlapping copies work. Caller queue_sound_command (an 8-byte command into the ring).
func_8002B80C.name: move_bytes

func_8002B880.about: Works out the audio frame size in samples: `fields` x `rate` / `refresh` rounded up to a multiple of 184 (0x8008D500), with smaller and larger ones 184 either side (0x8008D504, 0x8008D508) and the extra kept, size x `extra_percent` / 100 (0x8008D50C); returns the largest buffer needed (size + extra + 184). Only caller create_audio_manager. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_8002B880.name: set_audio_frame_sizes

func_8002B924.about: The sample count for the next audio frame from `queued` (samples still waiting to play): more than the extra + 184 queued gives the smaller size once, less than the extra the larger size, each only right after a frame in range (0x80053160 marks one), else the normal size (set_audio_frame_sizes). Caller func_8002B5B8 (the audio thread). (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_8002B924.name: next_audio_frame_size

func_8002B9B0.about: Builds the audio commands that mix the bus's voices: a clear of 0x2E0 bytes at 0x7C0 in DMEM (audio command 0x02, A_CLEARBUFF), then the envelope mixer of each of the bus's sources (+0x1C list, +0x14 count; n_al_envmixer_pull) at `sample_offset`, writing at `commands`. libultra n_alAuxBusPull by its role. Caller n_al_fx_pull. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_8002B9B0.name: n_al_aux_bus_pull

func_8002BA50.about: The unmodified n_alFxNew: picks the reverb parameter set by the configuration's effect type from libultra's presets (tables at 0x80053170, 0x800531D8, 0x80053260, 0x80053288, 0x800532B0 ..), allocates the delay line and sections (al_heap_alloc) and sets their filters (init_lpfilter, func_800308F0). Only caller n_al_syn_alloc_fx_stock; the game's copy is n_al_fx_new. func_80032240.name: al_envmixer_param

func_80032B80.name: al_resample_pull

func_80032D6C.about: The first audio library's resampler set-param handler (libultra alResampleParam, by its cases; n_al_resample_param is the second library's cut-down copy): 1 (AL_FILTER_SET_SOURCE) the source (+0); 4 (AL_FILTER_RESET) delta +0x20 = 0, first-frame +0x24 = 1, motion +0x30 = 0, unity pitch +0x1C = 0 and resets the source; 9 (AL_FILTER_START) motion +0x30 = 1 and starts the source; 7 (AL_FILTER_SET_PITCH) the ratio +0x18 = `param`; 8 (AL_FILTER_SET_UNITY_PITCH) +0x1C = 1; 2, 3, 5, 6 and others are passed to the source's handler. func_80032D6C.name: al_resample_param

func_80032E30.about: The first audio library's effects (reverb) pull (libultra alFxPull, by its callees; al_fx_new installs it at 0x80032E30): pulls the source (the aux bus) into DMEM 0x6C0, saves it into the delay line (fx_save_buffer), then for each section loads its input and output taps (fx_load_buffer, fx_load_output_buffer), mixes them by the section's gains (mixer commands 0x0C), filters through its low-pass when it has one (fx_filter_buffer) and saves the result back (fx_save_buffer); last moves the output back (0x0A) and steps the delay line's position. func_80035D50.about: Makes a float matrix that turns by `roll`, `pitch` and `heading` (degrees, made radians with the constant at 0x80053770, 0.0174533 = pi / 180), scales by `scale` and then moves to (`x`, `y`, `z`). It is libultra's guPositionF: the same arguments, and the same sums term by term ([0][0] = cos pitch cos heading x scale, [0][2] = -sin pitch x scale, the bottom row x, y, z, 1). (Confirmed 2026-11-12 against libultra's guPositionF.)
func_80035D50.name: gu_position_f

func_80035F28.about: gu_position_f made into a fixed-point Mtx: libultra's guPosition. (Confirmed 2026-11-12: the same sums as libultra's, term by term.)
func_80035F28.name: gu_position

func_80036110.about: The game's random numbers: the seed at 0x80053780 becomes ((seed * 4 + 2) * (seed * 4 + 3)) >> 2, and that is the result (in v0). Used wherever the game draws at random, such as the Superstar Select's Random (mod/src/variants.c).
func_80036110.name: next_random_number

func_80036140.about: Makes a float rotation matrix from roll, pitch and heading in degrees (made radians with the constant at 0x80053790). Matches libultra's guRotateRPYF. (Confirmed 2026-11-12: the same sums as libultra's, term by term.)
func_80036140.name: gu_rotate_rpy_f

func_800362C8.about: gu_rotate_rpy_f made into a fixed-point Mtx: libultra's guRotateRPY. (Confirmed 2026-11-12: the same sums as libultra's, term by term.)
func_800362C8.name: gu_rotate_rpy

func_80036460.about: The sine of an angle in radians (libultra's sinf). make_rotation_y puts it in a turn's [2][0].
func_80036460.name: sine

func_80036600.about: Compares `length` bytes at `a` and `b`, a word at a time when they're aligned alike; returns 0 when equal. libultra bcmp, by its code. Callers write_flash_page (verifying a write), write_save_block_if_changed, gb_pak_read_id and the pfs code.
func_80036600.name: compare_bytes

func_80036710.about: Copies `length` bytes from `source` to `destination`, correctly when the two overlap (from the end when the destination is above the source); a word at a time when both are aligned alike. Behaves as libultra's bcopy, with the same argument order (source first).
func_80036710.name: copy_memory

func_80036A30.about: Sets `length` bytes from `address` to zero, 32 bytes at a time in the middle. Behaves as libultra's bzero.
func_80036A30.name: zero_bytes

func_80036B28.about: The string printer's output step: copies `count` characters to `destination` (copy_bytes) and returns the place after them. libultra's sprintf output callback.
func_80036B28.name: sprintf_output

func_80037340.about: Creates the one-message queue (0x800BD930) that gives one thread at a time the serial interface (the controllers), and puts the one message in it. libultra's __osSiCreateAccessQueue, by its code.
func_80037340.name: si_create_access_queue

func_80037394.about: Waits until the serial interface is free and takes it: creates the access queue the first time, then waits for its message. libultra's __osSiGetAccess; the controller functions call it first.
func_80037394.name: si_get_access

func_80037400.about: Gives the serial interface back: puts the message back in the access queue. libultra's __osSiRelAccess.
func_80037400.name: si_release_access

func_80037430.about: The 5-bit CRC of a controller pak address, sent with each read or write of the pak. libultra's __osContAddressCrc, by its code.
func_80037430.name: cont_address_crc

func_8003749C.about: The 8-bit CRC of a 32-byte block read from or written to a controller pak. libultra's __osContDataCrc, by its code.
func_8003749C.name: cont_data_crc

func_80037800.about: Takes thread `thread` out of thread queue `queue` (linked through each thread's +0), wherever it is. libultra __osDequeueThread; enqueue_thread and pop_thread are its neighbours.
func_80037800.name: dequeue_thread

func_80037840.about: Gives up the processor: with interrupts off, marks the running thread (*0x800537D0) runnable (state 2) and goes through func_8003CDDC (the scheduler's enqueue and yield), then restores interrupts. It is libultra's osYieldThread (OS_STATE_RUNNABLE = 2, __osEnqueueAndYield on the run queue). (Confirmed 2026-11-12.)
func_80037840.name: yield_thread

func_80037A50.about: Starts the timer services: the current time 0x800A1120, base counter 0x80091C80 and VI interrupt count 0x8009FDEC cleared, and the timer list *0x800537E0 made empty (next and previous itself, interval, remaining, queue and message 0). libultra __osTimerServicesInit.
func_80037A50.name: timer_services_init

func_80037BE0.about: Arms the next timer interrupt: with interrupts off, the timer counter 0x800A8950 = osGetCount() and the compare register set from it plus the time (func_8003E290, __osSetCompare). libultra __osSetTimerIntr (the 468-count minimum is compiled to nothing here). Callers set_timer, timer_interrupt (the timer code).
func_80037BE0.name: set_timer_intr

func_80038050.about: libultra __viMgrMain: the VI manager thread's loop on its queue (`manager` +0xC): a retrace message (0xD) swaps the VI context (vi_swap_context), sends the retrace message every 'count' retraces (vi_get_next_context +2 / +0x10 / +0x14), counts retraces (0x8009FDEC) and adds the CPU count since the last one to the 64-bit time 0x800A1120; a counter message (0xE) runs the timer interrupt (timer_interrupt, func_80037AA4).
func_80038050.name: vi_manager_thread

func_800384B0.about: libultra __osViSwapContext: writes the next VI context (*0x80054BF4: its mode, frame buffer, x / y scale, features) to the VI registers 0xA4400004..0xA4400034 for the field the VI is in (0xA4400010 & 1), then makes it the current one (*0x80054BF0) and copies it into the other context. Callers vi_init and the VI manager (vi_manager_thread) at each retrace.
func_800384B0.name: vi_swap_context

func_80038820.about: Fills a 4 by 4 float matrix with the identity: 1.0 on the diagonal, 0 elsewhere. The floats are written as their bit patterns (0x3F800000 is 1.0).
func_80038820.name: make_identity_matrix

func_80038880.about: Converts a 4x4 float matrix to the RSP's fixed-point Mtx (16.16: the integer halves first, then the fractions). libultra's guMtxF2L.
func_80038880.name: gu_mtx_float_to_fixed

func_80038900.about: Multiplies two 4x4 float matrices: `result` = `a` x `b` (rows of a by columns of b, worked on the stack so `result` may be either). libultra guMtxCatF. Ten callers: the bone and model builders.
func_80038900.name: gu_mtx_cat_f

func_80038A00.about: Fills a 4 by 4 float matrix that scales by x, y and z. They arrive as bit patterns in integer registers.
func_80038A00.name: make_scale_matrix

func_80038A60.about: Scales the vector (x, y, z) in place to length 1. libultra's guNormalize.
func_80038A60.name: gu_normalize

func_80038AC0.about: Fills a 4 by 4 float matrix that moves by x, y and z. They arrive as bit patterns in integer registers.
func_80038AC0.name: make_translation_matrix

func_80038B20.about: Puts the point (x, y, z) through `matrix` (4x4 floats, rows, translation in the last row) and writes the result to out_x, out_y, out_z. The port uses it for a bone's offset from its parent (exe arcade_bones.cpp).
func_80038B20.name: transform_point

func_80038BD0.about: Starts a Transfer Pak on a controller channel (libultra osGbpakInit, by its arguments and its pak writes to 0x400 (address 0x8000, power) and 0x580 (0xB000, status)): (queue, pfs, channel). Callers open_transfer_pak, gb_pak_power, gb_pak_get_status.
func_80038BD0.name: gb_pak_init

func_80038DD0.about: Reads the Transfer Pak's status byte (address 0xB000) into `status` (libultra osGbpakGetStatus). Callers read_gb_cart_ram, write_gb_cart_ram, gb_pak_read_id.
func_80038DD0.name: gb_pak_get_status

func_80038EF0.about: Turns the Transfer Pak's cartridge power on or off (libultra osGbpakPower: pfs, flag). Callers close_transfer_pak, gb_pak_read_id and others.
func_80038EF0.name: gb_pak_power

func_80039010.about: Reads (`flag` 0) or writes (1) `size` bytes at Game Boy address `address` through the Transfer Pak (libultra osGbpakReadWrite, its bank switching through 0x600 = 0xC000). Callers enable_gb_cart_ram, read_gb_cart_ram, write_gb_cart_ram, gb_pak_read_id.
func_80039010.name: gb_pak_read_write

func_800391F0.about: Reads the Game Boy cartridge's header in the Transfer Pak into `id` (libultra osGbpakReadId: the logo checked with compare_bytes, the status to `status`). The game then checks the title (+0x34) and the company code (+0x44). Caller open_transfer_pak.
func_800391F0.name: gb_pak_read_id

func_80039430.about: libultra osGbpakCheckConnector, by its shape (as open_transfer_pak's about took it): with the Transfer Pak's status good (gb_pak_get_status, read twice when it says 0xD) and the cartridge powered (gb_pak_power(1) when status bit 0 is clear), reads the Game Boy cartridge's header area at 0x100.. in 32-byte blocks twice over (gb_pak_read_write) and compares the reads (compare_bytes), so a loose connector, which reads differently each time, is caught; the header's checksum is then checked. Returns 0 or a PFS error code. Caller open_transfer_pak. (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: gb_pak_get_status, read again when it gives 0xD, then the reads into the two 0x180-byte frame buffers; libultra gbpakcheckconnector.c's order.)
func_80039430.name: gb_pak_check_connector

func_80039C20.about: libultra osPfsAllocateFile, by its arguments and callees (as allocate_game_note's about took it): makes a note of `length` bytes (rounded up to 256-byte pages) with `company`, `game_code`, `game_name` and `ext_name` on the Controller Pak `pfs`: fails when one already exists (pfs_find_file) or there is too little room (pfs_free_blocks, func_8003ACF0), claims free pages bank by bank (pfs_declare_pages, linking the banks' chains, pfs_rw_inode), writes the new directory entry (cont_ram_write) and the note number to `*file_no`. Callers allocate_game_note, keep_pak_functions_linked.
func_80039C20.name: pfs_allocate_file

func_80039F2C.about: Claims up to page_count free pages (marked 3) of bank \bank in inode table inode for a new file, from the first data page (pfs +0x60, or 1 for banks after 0): chains them (each page points at the next, {bank, page}), counts them in *declared, stores the first in *\first_page (-1 when the bank has none) and, when the bank ran out first, the last in *last_page (else ends the chain with 1 and *last_page = 0). libultra __osPfsDeclearPage (its seven arguments). Caller pfs_allocate_file (osPfsAllocateFile).
func_80039F2C.name: pfs_declare_pages

func_8003A050.about: Deletes a Controller Pak note (libultra osPfsDeleteFile by its arguments (pfs, company, game code, name, extension) and its use of pfs_find_file and the pak's bank selection). (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: 5 (PFS_ERR_INVALID) for a zero company or game code, pfs_find_file, pfs_select_bank(0) for a multi-bank pak, cont_ram_read of the directory entry, then its pages freed through the inode; libultra pfsdeletefile.c's order.)
func_8003A050.name: pfs_delete_file

func_8003A1FC.about: Frees a file's pages in an inode table: from `start_page` of `bank`, marks each page 3 (unused) and follows the chain while the next page is in the same bank; stores the page it stopped at in `*last_page`. libultra __osPfsReleasePages. Caller pfs_delete_file.
func_8003A1FC.name: pfs_release_pages

func_8003A6B0.about: libultra osPfsFileState, by its shape: for note `file_no` of the Controller Pak `pfs` (below the note count +0x50, the pak set up, +0 & 1) reads its directory entry (cont_ram_read at the directory block +0x5C + file_no) and, when it is in use, follows its page chain through the inode tables (pfs_rw_inode per bank) to count its pages; writes to `state` the size (pages x 256), company (+8), game code (+4), extension (+0xA, 4 bytes) and name (+0xE, 16 bytes). Returns 0, 5 (PFS_ERR_INVALID) for a bad or empty note, 3 for a broken chain, or the device error; ends with func_8003B230 on the pak's queue and channel. Callers read_pak_notes, keep_pak_functions_linked.
func_8003A6B0.name: pfs_file_state

func_8003A850.about: libultra osPfsFindFile: looks through the Controller Pak's note table (pfs + 0x50 entries from block pfs + 0x5C) for the note with `company_code`, `game_code`, `game_name` and `ext_name`, writing its number to *`file_no`; returns a PFS error (5, PFS_ERR_INVALID, when there's none). The game looks for its own note with company '78' (0x3738) and game code 'NW4E' (0x4E573445; find_game_note).
func_8003A850.name: pfs_find_file

func_8003AA10.about: Finds which controllers have a pak plugged in: with the serial interface held (si_get_access), up to 3 tries of a status request through the pak buffer 0x800A9C30 (pfs_request_data 0, __osSiRawStartDma write then read, waiting on `queue`) read back by pfs_get_init_data, retrying while a channel reports an address CRC error (status bit 4); sets `*pattern` to the channels that answered without error with a pak in (status bit 0); returns the read DMA result. libultra osPfsIsPlug.
func_8003AA10.name: pfs_is_plug

func_8003AB8C.about: Fills the pak PIF buffer 0x800A9C30 (status word 0x800A9C6C = 1, last command 0x800A8758 = `command`) with a status request (send 1, receive 3) for each channel read (*0x800A10E4), then 0xFE. libultra __osPfsRequestData, the pak code's own copy of cont_pack_request_data. Caller pfs_is_plug.
func_8003AB8C.name: pfs_request_data

func_8003AC30.about: Reads the status replies from the pak PIF buffer 0x800A9C30 into `data` (type, status, error bits per channel) and `*pattern` (channels that answered), as cont_get_init_data does for 0x8009ECD0. libultra __osPfsGetInitData. Caller pfs_is_plug.
func_8003AC30.name: pfs_get_init_data

func_8003ACF0.about: libultra osPfsFreeBlocks (as read_pak_notes's about took it): counts the free pages (inode entries == 3) of every bank of the Controller Pak `pfs` (+0x64 banks; bank 0 from the first data page +0x60), reading each bank's inode table with pfs_rw_inode after pfs_check_id, and writes the free bytes (pages x 256) to `*bytes_free`. Returns 0, 5 (PFS_ERR_INVALID) when the pak is not set up, or the read error. Callers read_pak_notes, pfs_allocate_file, keep_pak_functions_linked.
func_8003ACF0.name: pfs_free_blocks

func_8003AE00.about: libultra osPfsNumFiles: writes the note table's size to *`max_files` and the number of notes in use (company and game code both set) to *`files_used`; returns a PFS error (5 when the pak isn't set up). Callers read_pak_notes and keep_pak_functions_linked (func_80005DE8).
func_8003AE00.name: pfs_num_files

func_8003AF00.about: libultra osPfsInitPak: sets up `pfs` for the Controller Pak on `channel` through `queue` (SI access around the first check, pfs_select_bank, the ID area read and its checksum via pfs_id_checksum). Returns a PFS error code (0 ok; 11, PFS_ERR_DEVICE, when the thing plugged in isn't a Controller Pak, which init_controller_pak checks for a Rumble Pak). Identified by its shape and calls; callers init_controller_pak, check_controller_pak and keep_pak_functions_linked (func_80005DE8).
func_8003AF00.name: pfs_init_pak

func_8003B0F8.about: Checks a Controller Pak's memory works: selects bank 0, saves block 0, writes the bytes 0..31 there, reads them back and compares (compare_bytes), then writes the saved block back; returns 11 (PFS_ERR_DEVICE) when they differ. libultra __osPfsCheckRamArea. Caller pfs_init_pak.
func_8003B0F8.name: pfs_check_ram_area

func_8003B1D0.about: Repairs a Controller Pak's ID: 5 (PFS_ERR_INVALID) unless the pak's status (+0) has bit 0 or bit 2 (& 5); else pfs_get_id on it and, when that succeeds (0), clears status bit 2 (the 4: ID broken). Returns the result. libultra osPfsRepairId by its shape. Callers keep_pak_functions_linked (the save code) and repair_save_pak_id. (2026-11-12, names2: confirmed from the lifted C++; the bit cleared is 4, bit 2.)
func_8003B1D0.name: pfs_repair_id

func_8003B320.about: Fills the pak PIF buffer 0x800A9C30 with a status request `command` (send 1, receive 3) for controller `channel` only: `channel` zero bytes (skipping the channels before it), the request, then 0xFE; last command 0x800A8758 = 0xFE. libultra __osPfsRequestOneChannel. Caller func_8003B230.
func_8003B320.name: pfs_request_one_channel

func_8003B3B4.about: libultra (__osContGetInitData's per-channel part): reads controller channel `channel`'s 6-byte reply from the SI buffer (0x800A9C30 + channel) into `cont_status` (OSContStatus): errno +3 = (byte 1 & 0xC0) >> 4, and when it is 0 the type +0 = byte 3 | byte 4 << 8 and the status byte +2 = byte 5. Caller func_8003B230.
func_8003B3B4.name: read_cont_status_reply

func_8003B440.about: Selects bank `bank` of a controller pak: fills a 32-byte block with the bank number and writes it to the pak's bank register. libultra's __osPfsSelectBank, by its code.
func_8003B440.name: pfs_select_bank

func_8003B4B0.about: Adds up a run of bytes and returns the low 16 bits of the total.
func_8003B4B0.name: sum_bytes

func_8003B4E4.about: The two checksums of a controller pak's 28-byte ID block: the sum of its 16-bit words into `checksum` and the sum of their complements into `inverted`. libultra's __osIdCheckSum, by its code.
func_8003B4E4.name: pfs_id_checksum

func_8003B528.about: libultra __osRepairPackId: writes a fresh ID block to the Controller Pak `pfs`: a new random-ish ID from osGetCount into `new_id`, works out the bank count by writing / reading back each bank's first block (pfs_select_bank, cont_ram_read / cont_ram_write; up to 0x20 banks, stopping where a bank mirrors bank 0), the checksums (pfs_id_checksum), then writes the copies to blocks 1, 3, 4 and 6 and reads block 1 back to check. Callers pfs_init_pak and pfs_get_id (when the ID is bad).
func_8003B528.name: pfs_repair_pack_id

func_8003B814.about: Looks for a good copy of a Controller Pak's ID block: reads the copies at blocks 1, 3, 4 and 6 into `id` until one's two checksums (the sum and the sum of complements of its 14 halfwords, at +0x1C / +0x1E) match, then writes it back over the bad copies. libultra __osCheckPackId. Callers pfs_init_pak, pfs_get_id (func_8003B978).
func_8003B814.name: pfs_check_pack_id

func_8003B978.about: libultra __osGetId: reads the Controller Pak's ID block (block 1, after selecting bank 0 if another is active) and checks its two checksums (pfs_id_checksum); a bad block is looked for elsewhere (pfs_check_pack_id) and repaired (pfs_repair_pack_id) when none is good (0xA) or when its +0x18 bit 0 is clear; then fills `pfs` from it (ID copy, bank count, inode / directory places). Returns 0 or the error. Callers pfs_repair_id and pfs_checker (func_8003E7E0) (osPfsInit's path).
func_8003B978.name: pfs_get_id

func_8003BB44.about: Checks the Controller Pak in `pfs` is still the same one: selects bank 0 when another is active (+0x65, retrying once), reads the ID block (block 1, again on error 2) and compares it with the ID kept at `pfs` +0xC; returns 2 (PFS_ERR_NEW_PACK) when it differs. libultra __osCheckId. Callers the pfs functions (pfs_find_file, pfs_num_files, ..).
func_8003BB44.name: pfs_check_id

func_8003BBFC.about: Reads (`flag` 0) or writes (1) the Controller Pak's inode table page for `bank` into / from `inode` (eight 32-byte blocks from block bank x 8 + 1, with its backup copy and the checksum byte +1 over the pages from the first data page +0x60), keeping the last one read in the cache 0x800A9478 (bank 0x80054AD4, channel 0x80054AD0). libultra __osPfsRWInode.
func_8003BBFC.name: pfs_rw_inode

func_8003BF40.about: Reads a 32-byte block of controller pak memory at `address` from controller `channel` into `buffer`, with the address and data CRCs, retrying on a CRC mismatch; holds the serial interface meanwhile. libultra's __osContRamRead.
func_8003BF40.name: cont_ram_read

func_8003C130.about: Writes a 32-byte block from `buffer` to controller pak memory at `address` on controller `channel`, with the address and data CRCs; holds the serial interface meanwhile. libultra's __osContRamWrite (its fifth argument forces writes to the reserved low pages).
func_8003C130.name: cont_ram_write

func_8003C3A0.about: libultra's osAfterPreNMI: set_signal_processor_start(0) (__osSpSetPc), so the signal processor can be reset after the reset button. Caller the scheduler thread scheduler_event_thread (func_80000E3C) on its pre-NMI message (0x29D), as libultra's scheduler does.
func_8003C3A0.name: after_pre_nmi

func_8003C3C0.about: Reads the PI bus timings of both domains (0xA4600014..0xA4600030: latency, pulse width, page size, release) into two PI handles' timing bytes in OSPiHandle order (+5 latency, +8 pulse, +6 page size, +7 release): domain 1 into 0x800A5FB0's, domain 2 into 0x8009ED28's, each with type +4 = 7. Taken to be the cartridge handles' set-up (libultra's osCartRomInit does this for domain 1). No converted callers. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_8003C3C0.name: pi_copy_bus_timings

func_8003C750.about: Does nothing, though the game still calls it. Probably what is left of something removed before release. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_8003C750.name: empty_8003C750

func_8003CEE4.about: Puts thread `thread` into the thread queue `queue` after every thread of the same or higher priority (+4). libultra's __osEnqueueThread, by its code.
func_8003CEE4.name: enqueue_thread

func_8003CF2C.about: Takes the first thread off the thread queue `queue` and returns it (in v0). libultra's __osPopThread, by its code.
func_8003CF2C.name: pop_thread

func_8003CF3C.about: Does nothing, though the game still calls it. Probably what is left of something removed before release. (2026-11-12, names4: confirmed from the lifted C++: the name says only what the code does).
func_8003CF3C.name: empty_8003CF3C

func_8003D0D0.about: Adds `mask` to the global interrupt mask (0x80054B00) with interrupts off meanwhile. libultra's __osSetGlobalIntMask, by its code.
func_8003D0D0.name: set_global_int_mask

func_8003D110.about: Removes `mask` from the global interrupt mask (0x80054B00), always keeping 0x401, with interrupts off meanwhile. libultra's __osResetGlobalIntMask, by its code.
func_8003D110.name: reset_global_int_mask

func_8003D160.about: libultra osPiRawStartDma: waits for the PI to be idle, sets the DRAM address (osVirtualToPhysical of `dram`) and the cartridge address (osRomBase *0x80000308 | `cart_address`, & 0x1FFFFFFF), then starts the transfer: `direction` 0 writes the read length (0xA460000C, ROM to RDRAM), 1 the write length (0xA4600008), `size` - 1; returns 0, or -1 for another direction. No converted caller.
func_8003D160.name: pi_raw_start_dma

func_8003D230.about: libultra's osPiGetCmdQueue: the PI device manager's command queue (*0x80053428), or NULL when the manager (0x80053420, __osPiDevMgr: +0 active, +8 the queue) isn't running. No converted callers.
func_8003D230.name: pi_get_command_queue

func_8003D250.about: libultra __osEPiRawReadIo: like epi_raw_write_io (PI idle wait, the domain's bus timings set when they differ), then reads the word at `handle` +0xC base | `address` | 0xA0000000 into *`data`. Returns 0. Callers epi_read_io, dev_mgr_main (func_8002EFC0).
func_8003D250.name: epi_raw_read_io

func_8003D3C0.about: libultra __osEPiRawWriteIo: waits for the PI to be idle (0xA4600010 & 3), sets the bus timings of `handle`'s domain (+9; latency, page size, release, pulse width +5..+8 into PI_BSD_DOMx registers 0xA4600014.. or 0xA4600024..) when they differ from the current ones (0x80053440[domain]), then writes `data` to `handle` +0xC base | `address` | 0xA0000000. Returns 0. Callers epi_write_io, dev_mgr_main (func_8002EFC0).
func_8003D3C0.name: epi_raw_write_io

func_8003D530.about: Writes the word `data` to `address` on the device of PI handle `handle`, holding the PI access lock (pi_get_access / pi_release_access) around the raw write epi_raw_write_io (func_8003D3C0) (which stores to the handle's base +0xC | address | 0xA0000000 after setting the bus timings). libultra osEPiWriteIo.

Modes 2-4 also set actors_load_at_once from actor 0's mode (2: off for -9 / -14; 3: on for -13 / -7; 4: on for -13 / -16). Each actor is handed its mode (0x801064B0 + actor x 4) and its cast costume (0x80106660 + actor x 4). Last, one scene actor a frame (front_end_frame_count & 3) gets +0x30C = 1, and 0x800F6368 = actor 0's mode (0x801056E0). Caller draw_front_end_frame. (2026-11-14, fablenames2: about rewritten from the code, read line by line: it listed the calls; the load flags, the per-actor arguments and the +0x30C mark were not in it.)

func_800F0DB8.about: The picture of `text` in the big font: its text texture record (find_text_texture_entry, func_80009E88), made when new: the font picture 0x1DA loaded (*0x80104C48), the string taken from `text` (with 0x40000000, the number in its low 22 bits written out with format_number), measured (measure_big_font_text), a cleared heap block for the 4-bit picture and the text drawn into it (draw_big_font_text). Kept in the menus' sprite cache (keep_text_texture_in_cache). Returns 0 when it can't be made. Caller draw_big_font_text_at.

Ten match AI callers, so a plan is not picked again too soon. (2026-11-12, names2: renamed from was_recent_move, the history holding the AI's plans.)

func_800F0E78.about: How many of the first `count` (at most 16) shorts of slot `slot`'s list at 0x80187DB0 + slot x 32 equal `value`: with `mode` 0 that count; any other mode gives 0 (mode 1 takes the count's sign bit, never set). The list is the one update_match_wrestlers_step clears at the match start and pushes into (15 entries moved down, the newest first) when a slot's value changes; the values asked for (0xD, 0xF, 0x1B, 0x6F, 0x9B) are wrestler states (27 the taunt, 111 / 155 the climb), so it counts how often he was lately in state `value`. All four match AI callers (ai_choose_on_apron_in_tag_match and others) pass mode 1, so their 'used lately' tests always see 0. (2026-11-12, names2: renamed from count_in_slot_list; read from the lifted C++.) (2026-11-12, names3: confirmed from the lifted C++: the count capped at 16 and the mode 0 / 1 returns exactly as said.)
func_800F0E78.name: count_recent_states

func_800F0EF0.about: The CPU's plan choice for the slot being decided (called by ai_plan_0_choose): first, while he takes punishment (his own state 21, 22, 45, 71, 73, 75, 86, 90, 92, 94, 96 or 99), each new such state (AI record +0x44 keeps the last) counts the AI record +0x5E down and at 0 sets a +0x80 bit and restarts it at a random 0-7; distance checks to the target and others with ai_press_c_right_when_free / ai_set_plan, +0x96 / state 129 cases; then, in a ring venue (the area 0x80159628 under 10; mod/src/arena_ringstage.c: 0-9 a ring, 10-19 a stage area, 20.. backstage), one chooser per place bit of the AI record +0x82 -- 1 / 2 ai_choose_in_ring, 4 ai_choose_in_ring_target_outside, 0x20 ai_choose_on_apron_target_outside, 8 ai_choose_on_apron_target_in_ring, 0x40 / 0x80 ai_choose_outside_target_in_ring, 0x10 ai_choose_both_on_apron, 0x2000 / 0x4000 / 0x8000 the cage-wall choosers -- and outside a ring venue ai_choose_away_from_ring; then the SPECIAL-ready choosers by the two men's +0x82 & 0x3C0, ai_choose_in_ladder_match (func_800FC810) when 0x80097EC0 & 0x100000, the plan 0x90 for a CPU in the ring with two out (ai_self_in_with_two_out) whose target has +0x94 & 1, ai_choose_elsewhere for the place bit 0x100 (ring venues), and with no 0x800A9950 rule bit a situation (+0x48) of 15-20 may hold buttons 2 (ai_object_within_reach, func_800FCAFC).

Sets plans (ai_set_plan, 8 places), tries the corner plan, the armed-target defence and the plan steps ai_choose_at_target_in_corner (func_800F75A8) / ai_react_to_target_up_top (func_800F7BFC) / ai_choose_from_distance (func_800F7DB0) / ai_should_tag_partner (func_800FB4C0) by chance and distance. func_800F1760.about: Story panel kind 3 (draw_story_panels, func_800F2028) at (`x`, `y`): the box picture 0x1D9 (0x48 x 0x30 with `flags` & 1, else 0x30 x 0x20) and the money 0x80097ED8 in it (number_digits_text, lettering 0x8030, draw_image_in_tiles_scaled); with `flags` & 1 and 0x80097EDC set (not -1) also the amount before (0x80097EE0) and '+' with the money won (0x80097EDC) above it, as finish_story leaves them.
